rows.title: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) - FAQs and General Observations / Guidelines for filing of BRSR
rows.desc: Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No: NSE/CML/2024/11 Date: May 10, 2024 To, The Company Secretary(ies) Listed Companies Subject: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) – FAQs & General Observations / Guidelines for filing of BRSR. Dear Sir / Madam, This has reference to Regulation 34 (2) (f) of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 and SEBI vide Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-SEC-2/P/CIR/2023/122 dated July 12, 2023, which requires Top One Thousand listed entities based on market capitalization, to submit BRSR as per the updated format as specified by SEBI. In this regard, please find annexed the BRSR FAQs / Guidelines & General Observations based on filing of BRSR for last year. The Companies are requested to comply with the requirement of listing regulations and other applicable regulations as amended from time to time. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. Apeksha Raichura Manager - Listing Encl: Annexure - FAQs Disclaimer: These guidelines are issued as guidance only. The directions / instructions issued in the provision of Law, Regulation, SEBI, and Exchange circular are referred to in these guidelines are final for decision making in the matter. These guidelines are not and should not be construed as substitution / clarification / explanation on any matter on which provision of Law, Regulation or SEBI / Exchange circular were issued. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS / GENERAL OBSERVATIONS & GUIDELINES ON FILING OF BUSINESS RESPONSIBILITY AND SUSTAINABILITY REPORT (BRSR / BRSR Core) PART 1 - FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS 1. Which listed Companies are mandatorily required to file BRSR? Top one thousand listed Companies based on market capitalization shall mandatorily submit BRSR in the format as specified by the SEBI vide Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-SEC- 2/P/CIR/2023/122 dated July 12, 2023. Link of market capitalization as on March 31, 2024, is given below: https://www.nseindia.com/regulations/listing-compliance/nse-market-capitalisation-all- companies For e.g. If the listed Companies are falling under top one thousand listed Companies based on market capitalization as on March 31, 2024, filing of BRSR shall be applicable to them for the Financial Year 2023-24. 2. If the Company is not falling under top one thousand listed Companies based on market capitalization as on March 31, 2024, but the Company was falling under top one thousand listed Companies based on market capitalization as on March 31, 2023, or March 31, 2022, will BRSR be applicable to the Company for March 31, 2024, pursuant to Regulation 3 (2) of SEBI LODR, 2015? Pursuant to Regulation 3(2) of the SEBI LODR, 2015 - The provisions of these regulations which become applicable to listed companies on the basis of market capitalisation criteria shall continue to apply to such companies even if they fall below such thresholds. The listed companies are requested to comply with the existing Regulation. 3. Can the listed Companies which do not form part of top one thousand listed Companies file BRSR on a voluntary basis? Yes, listed Companies which do not form part of top one thousand listed Companies including the Companies which have listed their specified securities on the SME Exchange, may voluntarily submit BRSR. 4. If the listed Company is in top one thousand market capitalization list of NSE & not in top one thousand market capitalization list of BSE or vice versa. Whether the applicability for filing BRSR is with NSE / BSE only or with NSE & BSE together? If the listed Company is in the top one thousand market capitalization list on any Exchange, then the listed Company is required to file BRSR with both the Exchanges. 5. Which listed Companies are mandatorily required to obtain Reasonable Assurance on BRSR Core? Top 150 listed Companies based on market capitalization as on March 31, 2024, shall mandatorily obtain Reasonable Assurance of BRSR Core as specified by the SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-SEC-2/P/CIR/2023/122 dated July 12, 2023. If the listed Companies have obtained assurance and selects “Yes” under “Whether the company has undertaken reasonable assurance of BRSR Core?” in BRSR utility, then it shall be mandatory to provide details of Point 15 i.e. Name of assurance provider & Point 16 i.e. Type of assurance obtained, in the BRSR utility. If listed Companies select “All / Partial” option under Point 16 in the BRSR utility, then the listed Companies need to specify whether the assurance obtained is “Reasonable Assurance” or “Limited Assurance”. Also, a copy of Reasonable Assurance Certificate is mandatorily to be attached along with the BRSR while submitting PDF & Annual Report with the Exchanges. 6. Whether the BRSR XBRL utility at the BSE portal can be used for uploading at NSE NEAPS portal and vice-versa? Yes, listed Companies can use either of NSE or BSE BRSR XBRL utility to upload at either of the Exchanges. The utilit
rows.summary:
This circular from NSE (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2024/11 dated May 10, 2024) is a guidance note for listed companies on filing the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) and BRSR Core, and it reiterates that the controlling requirements are the SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015 and SEBI Circular dated July 12, 2023 (SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-SEC-2/P/CIR/2023/122). The main filing obligation remains that the **top 1,000 listed companies by market capitalization** must submit BRSR in the **updated SEBI-prescribed format**; for example, if a company is in the top 1,000 as of **March 31, 2024**, BRSR applies for **FY 2023–24**. NSE also clarifies that if a company was previously within the top 1,000 on **March 31, 2023 or March 31, 2022**, the obligation continues even if it later falls below the threshold, because Regulation 3(2) preserves applicability once triggered by market-cap criteria. Companies outside the top 1,000 may still file BRSR **voluntarily**, including companies listed on the **SME Exchange**.

For exchange filing, NSE states that if a company is in the top 1,000 on **any one exchange** (NSE or BSE), it must file BRSR with **both exchanges**, not just the exchange where it appears in the top-1,000 list. The circular also addresses BRSR Core assurance requirements: the **top 150 listed companies by market capitalization as of March 31, 2024** must mandatorily obtain **Reasonable Assurance** on BRSR Core. If a company indicates in the BRSR utility that it has undertaken reasonable assurance, it must complete the assurance-provider details at **Point 15** and the **type of assurance** at **Point 16**; if “All / Partial” is selected for Point 16, the company must further specify whether the assurance is **Reasonable Assurance** or **Limited Assurance**. A **copy of the Reasonable Assurance Certificate** must be attached when submitting the BRSR PDF and annual report to the exchanges.

NSE also notes a practical filing rule: the **BRSR XBRL utility from either NSE or BSE can be used interchangeably** for uploading at either exchange, so companies are not restricted to the utility of the same exchange where they file. The annexed FAQs/guidelines are expressly described as **guidance only** and do not override the underlying law, SEBI regulations, or exchange circulars; companies must continue to comply with all applicable listing and other regulatory requirements as amended from time to time.

rows.title: SCORES 2.0 New Technology to strengthen SEBI Complaint Redressal System for Investors
rows.desc: Non-Confidential To all Listed Companies / Municipal Debt Securities /Registrars and Share Transfer Agents Subject: SCORES 2.0 New Technology to strengthen SEBI Complaint Redressal System for Investors Exchange vide Circular No. NSE/ISC/58504 dated September 21, 2023, and Circular No. NSE/ISC/59602 dated December 01, 2024, had informed the Market participants with respect to SEBI circular no. SEBI/HO/OIAE/IGRD/CIR/P/2023/156 dated September 20, 2023, on Redressal of Investor Grievances through the SEBI Complaint Redressal (SCORES) Platform. In continuation to the same, SEBI vide its press release no. PR No.06/2024 dated April 01, 2024, has informed that the new version of the SEBI Complaint Redress System (SCORES 2.0) has been launched w.e.f. April 01, 2024. A Copy of the release is attached herewith as Annexure A, which is self-explanatory. All Listed Companies / Municipal Debt Securities /Registrars and Share Transfer Agents are required to note and adhere to the below: 1. SCORES user ID and Password details are being sent to the e-mail ID of the respective contact person, by SEBI. 2. Upon receipt of the “Complaint” through SCORES, Listed Company/ Municipal Debt Securities/Registrars and Share Transfer shall resolve the complaint within 21 calendar days and submit Action taken Report (ATR) vide SCORES. The submitted ATR will be automatically routed to the complainant. 3. In case complainant is not satisfied with the resolution, the said complaint will be escalated to the Exchange, for review. Such escalated complaints are required to be addressed by the Exchange within 10 calendar days. 4. Subsequent to the first review by the Exchange, if the investor still remains dissatisfied with the resolution, they can escalate the complaint for a second review to SEBI. 5. In case of nonadherence to the prescribed timelines by the Listed Company/ Municipal Debt Securities/Registrars and Share Transfer or the Designated Body as the case may be, the complaint will be auto escalated to the next level. Department: INVESTOR SERVICES CELL Circular Ref. No: NSE/CML/2024/09 Date: April 05, 2024 Continuation Sheet Non-Confidential 6. At any stage, Investor will have an option to refer the complaint to ODR (Online Dispute Resolution). Once the Complaint has been referred to ODR, the same shall be treated as disposed of in SCORES 2.0. 7. All Listed Companies shall take note of Schedule VI of the SEBI circular no. SEBI/HO/OIAE/IGRD/CIR/P/2023/156 dated September 20, 2023, read with SEBI circular no. SEBI/HO/OIAE/IGRD/CIR/P/2023/183 dated December 01, 2023, for timelines for handling of complaints and actions in case of non-compliances. All are requested to take note of the contents of the aforesaid circular. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Jinit Thakkar Vice President Toll Free No Email id 1800 266 0050 (select option 5) ignse@nse.co.in
rows.summary:
This circular informs listed companies, municipal debt securities issuers, and registrars and share transfer agents that SEBI’s upgraded complaint-handling platform, SCORES 2.0, has been launched effective April 1, 2024, and that the SEBI complaint redress framework must now be followed on that system. SEBI will send the SCORES user ID and password to the e-mail address of each entity’s designated contact person, so firms should ensure the correct contact details are on record and monitored.

For any complaint received through SCORES, the listed company / municipal debt securities entity / RTA must resolve the matter within 21 calendar days and upload the Action Taken Report (ATR) in SCORES; the ATR is then automatically forwarded to the complainant. If the complainant is dissatisfied, the complaint is escalated to the Exchange for first-level review, and the Exchange must address that escalated complaint within 10 calendar days. If the investor remains dissatisfied after the Exchange’s review, the complaint may be escalated to SEBI for a second review.

The circular also makes clear that failure by the listed company / municipal debt securities entity / RTA, or by the Designated Body as applicable, to meet the prescribed timelines will cause the complaint to be auto-escalated to the next level. In addition, at any stage the investor may choose to refer the complaint to ODR (Online Dispute Resolution); once referred to ODR, the complaint is treated as disposed of in SCORES 2.0. Listed companies are specifically directed to note Schedule VI of SEBI circular SEBI/HO/OIAE/IGRD/CIR/P/2023/156 dated September 20, 2023, together with SEBI circular SEBI/HO/OIAE/IGRD/CIR/P/2023/183 dated December 1, 2023, for the complaint-handling timelines and the consequences for non-compliance.

rows.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) – Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Extending framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level to all listed companies in a phased manner
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2024/08 Date: March 28, 2024 To All Listed Companies, Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) – Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Extending framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level to all listed companies in a phased manner. This has reference to NSE Circular no. NSE/CML/2024/03 dated January 30, 2024, NSE/CML/2023/79 dated November 17, 2023, NSE/CML/2022/40 dated August 05, 2022, NSE/CML/2023/49 dated June 28, 2023 and NSE/CML/2023/59 dated July 31, 2023 and in accordance with Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) circular no. SEBI/HO/ISD/ISD-SEC-4/P/CIR/2022/107 dated August 5, 2022 and SEBI/HO/ISD/ISD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/124 dated July 19, 2023, regarding Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level. Please find annexed the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on aforementioned SEBI circulars. Companies are requested to comply with the requirements of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 and other applicable regulations as amended from time to time. The FAQs can be referred only for guidance purpose. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Manasi Sawant Senior Manager FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS 1. Who can update the Trading window closure period? Ans. Currently, the NIFTY 50 / SENSEX 30 and TOP 2000 companies as per BSE market capitalization for quarter ending December 2023 which will be further extended rest all listed companies from 1st April 2024. 2. Whether the issuer (listed entity) needs to update member details to depositories again for the purpose of Trading window closure period? Ans. No. the member / designated person (DP) data already uploaded for the purpose of System Driven Disclosure (SDD), will be automatically populated to users for updating Trading window closure period in the system. 3. Depositories system will be effective from October 1, 2023. So, will the system allow us to enter the data in the last week of September? Ans. Issuer can enter the trading window closure period i.e. start date and end date till T-2 days of respective dates. 4. End Date will be modifiable in depositories system? How to put end date of Closure of Trading Window, if Date of Board meeting has not been decided on 1st day of Quarter? Ans. Yes, the end date will be modifiable. Issuer can put a notional end date initially and once the board meeting date is decided it can be modified on basis of T-2 days. 5. Can pledge invoke happen during the tenure of PAN freeze? Ans. No, Pledge invoking is not allowed in tenure of PAN freeze, unless pledge is marked before the trading window closure period. 6. If there are multiple accounts, in both depositories whether both depositories freeze the PAN? Ans. Freezing is done on PAN – ISIN level basis, if client PAN have multiple accounts in both depositories, it will freeze on both depositories basis on the PAN uploaded in SDD data for DPs with Designated Depository only. The DPs details needs to be updated only with Designated Depository and not on both depositories. 7. As per the circular the SDD monitoring is effective immediately from the 1st day of the month following the end of quarter. There are companies which have trading window closure date prior to 1st day of month following end of quarter. How do those companies deal with the update. Should we necessarily put the trading window closure date as 1st of the month? Ans. Currently in portal shall update 1st day of the month following the end of quarter and it recorded same as in both depositories. If there are any companies which have trading window closure date prior to 1st day of month following end of quarter, issuer need to update record on internal basis at their end. 8. If during trading window, issuer (listed entity) removed DP from the list due to cessation. Do they need to again delete from Trading Window tab as well, if yes, request you to please link this will addition deletion column? Ans. Issuer can delete DP name from the list, but it will not be removed from trading window closure period. Issuers need to give exemption period for the same to that DP or else it will be unfrozen after the trading window period ends. 9. Can listed entity update addition of DP in during trading window closure period? Ans. Yes, listed entity can update addition of DP in depositories system during trading window closure period. But the freeze date will be accepted on T-2 basis from the date of addition. 10. What happens when the Listing trading approval for ESOP allotment is approved by the Exchanges during the
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated March 28, 2024 issues FAQs on the SEBI trading-window/PAN-freeze framework under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of the PIT Regulations, and says the FAQs are for guidance only while listed companies must continue complying with the PIT Regulations and any amendments. It extends the system-based restriction on trading by Designated Persons (DPs) through freezing PANs at the security level to all listed companies in a phased rollout: as of this FAQ set, the system is already available for NIFTY 50 / SENSEX 30 companies and the top 2000 companies by BSE market capitalization for the quarter ended December 2023, with the remaining listed companies to be covered from 1 April 2024. The issuer does not need to re-enter DP/member data for this purpose if it was already uploaded for System Driven Disclosure (SDD), because that data will auto-populate into the trading-window module.

Operationally, issuers can enter trading-window closure start and end dates only up to T-2 days of the relevant dates, and if the board meeting date is not known on day one of the quarter they may enter a notional end date and later modify it, again subject to the T-2 rule. The depository system is intended to record trading-window closure from the first day of the month following quarter-end for SDD monitoring, so if a company’s actual closure period begins earlier than that, the company must maintain that earlier date internally even though the portal records the first-day-of-next-month date. The PAN freeze works on a PAN–ISIN basis and, where a DP has multiple accounts across both depositories, the freeze will apply across both depositories based on the PAN data uploaded in SDD for the DP, using only the designated depository; DPs do not need to be updated on both depositories.

The FAQs also clarify that pledge invocation is not permitted during the PAN-freeze period unless the pledge was marked before the trading-window closure began. If a DP ceases during a closure period and is deleted from the list, that deletion does not automatically remove the PAN freeze from the trading-window record; the issuer must either grant an exemption period for that DP or the freeze will lift only when the trading-window closure ends. New DPs can be added during the closure period, but the freeze date for the addition will be accepted only on a T-2 basis from the date of addition. The document begins to address ESOP-related trading approval, but the provided text cuts off before the answer is completed, so no further rule can be reliably summarized from the excerpt.

rows.title: Corporate Grouping of Listed Companies
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Download Ref No: NSE/CML/2024/07 Date: March 27, 2024 To All Listed Companies, Sub: Corporate Grouping of Listed Companies This is in reference to the NSE Circular Ref. No. NSE/CML/2023/81 dated November 30, 2023 regarding Corporate Grouping of Listed Companies. It was informed by the Exchange that in case of any change in corporate group of any listed company pursuant to any event such as Corporate Restructuring, Takeover, Merger, Demerger, Acquisition, Delisting etc., the companies are required to intimate the Exchange within Two Working Days of the Effective Date of the change. In this regard, it is to be noted that the Exchange has introduced an online module to facilitate the listed companies to file the intimation of change of its corporate group through NEAPS application (Link: https://neaps.nseindia.com/NEWLISTINGCORP/login.jsp). Therefore, henceforth the companies are required to intimate the change in their corporate group within Two Working Days of the Effective Date of the change through the online module only in NEAPS application. The path of the module and procedure to change the corporate group is annexed hereby as an Annexure. It may be noted that the corporate group repository has been formulated only for the purpose of compliance with SEBI Circular No. SEBI/ HO/ AFD/ AFD –PoD –2/ CIR/ P/ 2023/148 dated August 24, 2023 and should not be considered as a legal interpretation/ definition of the terms such as ‘group/ related party/ associate companies’ mentioned in any other SEBI Regulation/ Circular/ Act etc. The listed companies are requested to take note of the aforementioned disclosure requirements and exercise abundant precaution while identifying and intimating its Corporate Group. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Manasi Sawant Senior Manager National Stock Exchange of India Annexure Procedure to intimate change of Corporate Group– Path – NEAPS login > Compliance > Disclosures > Corporate Grouping FPI In case the field ‘Corporate Grouping FPI’ is not visible, click on ‘Customize Menu’ (on top-right of the home page of NEAPS) and click on the check box of ‘Corporate Grouping FPI’. A print screen of the same is as below: - National Stock Exchange of India To change the Corporate Group of the company, send the request by clicking on ‘Modify’-
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has reiterated and tightened the process for reporting changes in a listed company’s corporate group. Under the earlier circular referenced in the notice, any change in a listed company’s corporate group arising from events such as corporate restructuring, takeover, merger, demerger, acquisition, or delisting must be intimated to the Exchange within **two working days of the effective date** of the change.

The key update in this March 27, 2024 circular is procedural: **from now on, companies must submit this intimation only through NSE’s online NEAPS module**, rather than by any other method. NSE says it has introduced an online filing module in the NEAPS application for this purpose, and the annexure provides the path to the function: **NEAPS login > Compliance > Disclosures > Corporate Grouping FPI**. If the menu item is not visible, users must go to **“Customize Menu”** at the top right of the NEAPS home page and tick the checkbox for **“Corporate Grouping FPI.”** The annexure also notes that the change request is initiated by clicking **“Modify.”**

NSE further clarifies that this corporate group repository exists **only to support compliance with SEBI Circular No. SEBI/ HO/ AFD/ AFD –PoD –2/ CIR/ P/ 2023/148 dated August 24, 2023**, and it is **not** a legal definition or interpretation of terms such as “group,” “related party,” or “associate companies” under any other SEBI regulation, circular, or act. For compliance teams, the practical obligation is to carefully determine whether a corporate event has changed the company’s group classification, and if so, ensure the NEAPS filing is made within the two-working-day deadline after the effective date, using the new online workflow only.

rows.title: Repeal of circular(s) outlining procedure to deal with cases where securities are issued prior to April 01, 2014, involving offer / allotment of securities to more 49 but up to 200 investors in a financial year
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Download Ref No: NSE/CML/2024/06 Date: March 14, 2024 To, All Listed Entities Subject: Repeal of circular(s) outlining procedure to deal with cases where securities are issued prior to April 01, 2014, involving offer / allotment of securities to more 49 but up to 200 investors in a financial year This is with reference to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/ 016 dated March 13, 2024, titled ‘Repeal of circular(s) outlining procedure to deal with cases where securities are issued prior to April 01, 2014, involving offer / allotment of securities to more than 49 but up to 200 investors in a financial year.’ A copy of the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website (https://www.nseindia.com/companies- listing/circular-for-listed-companies-equity-market) for your reference. You are requested to please take note of the same and ensure compliance. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Charmi Dharod Senior Manager Encl: SEBI Circular
rows.summary:
The NSE circular dated March 14, 2024 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2024/06) is a notice to all listed entities informing them that SEBI has issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/016 dated March 13, 2024, which repeals earlier circular(s) that had set out a procedure for handling cases where securities were issued before April 1, 2014 and the issuer had offered/allotted securities to more than 49 but up to 200 investors in a financial year. In practical terms, this means the prior special procedure for addressing those legacy pre-April 1, 2014 issuance situations is withdrawn, and listed entities should no longer rely on or follow the repealed circular(s) for such cases. The notice does not introduce a new substantive filing process, deadline, threshold, or numerical change beyond referencing the affected investor range of more than 49 up to 200 investors and the relevant cutoff date of April 1, 2014.

For compliance purposes, the key action is simply to take note of the repeal and ensure alignment with the updated SEBI position, with the NSE directing listed entities to review the SEBI circular available on its website and comply accordingly. The document itself does not specify any new reporting obligation, transition timeline, or enforcement mechanism; it is an informational circular confirming the repeal and advising entities to ensure compliance with the changed regulatory framework.

rows.title: Revised Pricing Methodology for Institutional Placements of Privately Placed Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT)
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Download Ref No: NSE/CML/2024/05 Date: February 09, 2024 To, All Infrastructure Investment Trusts (“InvITs”) All Parties to InvITs Subject: Revised Pricing Methodology for Institutional Placements of Privately Placed Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT). This is with reference to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-PoD/P/CIR/2024/10 dated February 08, 2024 titled “ Revised Pricing Methodology for Institutional Placements of Privately Placed Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT)” A copy of the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website (https://www.nseindia.com/companies- listing/circular-for-listed-companies-equity-market) for your reference. You are requested to please take note of the same and ensure compliance. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Charmi Dharod Senior Manager Encl: SEBI Circular
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued Circular NSE/CML/2024/05 on February 9, 2024, addressed to all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and all parties to InvITs, directing them to note and comply with SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-PoD/P/CIR/2024/10 dated February 8, 2024, titled “Revised Pricing Methodology for Institutional Placements of Privately Placed Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT).” The NSE circular itself does not restate the detailed pricing mechanics; it serves as a forwarding/compliance notice pointing recipients to the SEBI circular for the substantive requirements.  

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the pricing methodology for institutional placements of privately placed InvITs has been revised, and affected InvITs and all related transaction parties are expected to follow the revised SEBI framework immediately upon the SEBI circular’s issuance on February 8, 2024, unless the underlying SEBI text specifies a different implementation date. rows.title: Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Extending framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level to all listed companies in a phased manner
rows.summary:
The document is an NSE circular dated 30 January 2024 that expands the existing “trading window closure” / anti-insider-trading controls under Clause 4 of Schedule B of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. Its key change is the phased extension of a mechanism that restricts trading by Designated Persons by “freezing” their PAN at the security level, so that the restriction is no longer limited to select companies but is rolled out to all listed companies over time.

For compliance purposes, the circular means listed entities must align their insider-trading controls with this PAN-based security-level freeze framework, which is intended to prevent Designated Persons from trading in company securities during trading window closure periods even through accounts or relationships outside the immediate company system. The circular is specifically tied to the trading-window closure obligations already required under Clause 4 of Schedule B and Regulation 9 of the PIT Regulations, so it does not create a completely new statutory concept, but it does require implementation of a more technical enforcement method. The affected parties are all listed companies, though the rollout is phased rather than immediate for everyone, so compliance teams need to determine when their company falls into the phase applicable under NSE’s implementation schedule and ensure systems/processes are updated accordingly.

The practical compliance obligation is to ensure PAN-linked restrictions are activated at the security level for Designated Persons, which implies coordination with depositories, intermediaries, and internal compliance systems so trades are blocked during trading window closure periods. Companies should expect that this requires accurate PAN capture and maintenance for all Designated Persons, monitoring of trading windows, and procedures to respond to any system-blocked transactions or exception handling in line with insider trading policy. The document’s substance is therefore an implementation extension: it broadens the freeze-based trading restriction model to all listed companies and requires listed entities to prepare for system-level enforcement rather than relying only on manual controls.

rows.title: Filing of Announcements pertaining to Loss of Share Certificate/Issue of Duplicate Share Certificate/Closure of Trading Window and Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (''CIRP’) in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform
rows.desc: Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/85 Date: December 08, 2023 To, The Company Secretary/ Compliance Officer, All Listed Companies Subject: Filing of Announcements pertaining to Loss of Share Certificate/Issue of Duplicate Share Certificate/Closure of Trading Window and Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (‘CIRP’) in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform. Further to the various Exchange circulars (Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/34 dated May 15, 2023, Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/28 dated March 31, 2023, Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/11 dated January 27, 2023) issued for filing of equity announcement in XBRL mode and other circulars seeking comments/feedback from listed entities on the captioned events (Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/40 dated June 14, 2023 and NSE/CML/2023/41 dated June 21, 2023), kindly note the facility for filings disclosures intimating the following announcements under SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘SEBI LODR’) will be made available in XBRL format with effect from December 09, 2023 (‘effective date’) 1) Loss of Share Certificate/Issue of Duplicate Share Certificate 2) Closure of Trading Window 3) Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process At the initial stage, the PDF filings will be considered by the Exchange as compliance under Regulation 30 of the SEBI LODR. Further, all listed entities would be required to also submit the filings in XBRL mode within 24 hours of submission of the said PDF filing. At a later stage (date to be informed separately) Exchange will shift to only XBRL submission. It may be noted that, XBRL utility for the above-mentioned subjects is available at the path COMPLIANCE >> Common XBRL Upload >> Equity Announcement- XBRL, basis the selection of the ‘Subject of Announcement’. Further, it may be noted that the aforesaid three events, will be made available in iXBRL format to the listed entities and it will be made available to the listed entities at the path Report >> Announcement XBRL Report iXBRL or Inline XBRL, is an open standard that enables a single document to provide both human-readable and structured, machine-readable data. iXBRL takes the HTML standard that is used to power the world’s web pages and embeds extra “tags” into it that give meaning to the figures and statements in a format that can be understood by a computer. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Ajit Mahadik Manager – Listing Compliance Please refer the below steps/path for submitting the announcements in XBRL format for the abovementioned subjects: 1. Post logging in the NEAPS portal (https://neaps.nseindia.com/NEWLISTINGCORP) - go to COMPLIANCE >> Common XBRL Upload 2. On the Common XBRL Upload, please select Equity Announcement-XBRL from the drop down under Module: 3. On clicking the Equity Announcement- XBRL, the user shall then select the Subject of the Announcement from the drop down: 4. On selection of the any respective subject, the user can download the XBRL utility for the said subject from the table below (“Download Offline Excel Utilities) and fill-in the utility and generate the XML file. For Duplicate/Loss For Trading Window For CIRP related events: 5. Once the XML is generated from the utility, fill-in the required details on the portal and click on the Upload XBRL File and complete the submission. In case any queries concerning the captioned subject, please reach out to the Announcements team at takeover@nse.co.in or on the contact details given on NEAPS platform. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Ajit Mahadik Manager – Listing Compliance
rows.summary:
This NSE Listing circular, dated **December 8, 2023** and addressed to the **Company Secretary/Compliance Officer of all listed companies**, announces that certain **Regulation 30** disclosures under the **SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015** must now be filed in **XBRL format** on the **NEAPS** platform for three specific announcement types: **loss of share certificate/issue of duplicate share certificate**, **closure of trading window**, and **Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP)**. The new XBRL filing facility becomes available from **December 9, 2023**; from that date, companies should use the XBRL utility in NEAPS for these subjects, accessible via **COMPLIANCE → Common XBRL Upload → Equity Announcement-XBRL**, after selecting the relevant “Subject of Announcement.”

The circular also imposes a **dual-filing requirement during the initial stage**: the **PDF filing will be treated by NSE as compliance under Regulation 30**, but the listed entity must **also submit the same disclosure in XBRL mode within 24 hours of the PDF submission**. NSE states that this is only an interim arrangement and that, at a **later date to be separately notified**, the Exchange will move to **XBRL-only submission** for these events. Listed entities must therefore ensure both the initial PDF filing and the follow-on XBRL upload are completed on time until the transition date is announced.

Operationally, the process requires the user to log in to the **NEAPS portal** at the listed URL, navigate to the XBRL upload module, choose the applicable announcement subject, **download the offline Excel utility**, complete it, and **generate an XML file** for upload. After XML generation, the filer must enter the required details on the portal and click **“Upload XBRL File”** to finish submission. NSE also notes that these three events will be available in **iXBRL format**, and the report can be accessed in NEAPS under **Report → Announcement XBRL Report iXBRL or Inline XBRL**; the circular provides a general explanation that iXBRL combines human-readable HTML with machine-readable tags.

For support or clarification, listed entities are directed to contact the **Announcements team at takeover@nse.co.in** or use the contact details shown on the NEAPS platform. The circular is issued by **National Stock Exchange of India Limited**, signed by **Ajit Mahadik, Manager – Listing Compliance**.

rows.title: Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Extending framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level to all listed companies in a phased manner - Next 1,000 companies in terms of BSE Market Capitalization as of June 30, 2023 for PIT - Trading Window Closure Period
rows.summary:
This document is a SEBI/PIT trading-window compliance communication that extends the “freeze PAN at security level” framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) to additional listed companies in a phased rollout. The specific cohort covered here is the next 1,000 listed companies ranked by BSE market capitalization as of June 30, 2023; these companies are being brought into the trading-window closure/freeze mechanism under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. Practically, this means the affected listed entities must ensure that DPs’ PANs are frozen at the security level so that trading in the company’s securities is blocked during trading-window closure periods, rather than relying only on manual self-declaration or traditional restrictions.

For compliance teams at affected companies, the key obligation is operational readiness to implement the PAN-level freeze mechanism for all relevant DPs and to align internal insider-trading controls, broker/depository instructions, and trading-window closure processes with this framework. The document is explicitly part of a phased expansion to all listed companies, so even if a company is not in this first covered group it should expect eventual inclusion and should prepare systems and procedures accordingly. The document title indicates this is specifically about the “Trading Window Closure Period,” so the requirement is tied to blackout periods under the PIT Regulations and affects trading by DPs during those closure windows. The attached Annexure I workbook appears to contain the implementation list/details, but the substantive regulatory point is the phased extension of security-level PAN freezing for the stated next 1,000 companies as of the June 30, 2023 market-cap ranking.

Dear Sir/ Madam, This is with reference to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-RAC- 1/P/CIR/2023/178 dated November 08, 2023, issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) titled “Procedural framework for dealing with unclaimed amounts lying with Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and manner of claiming such amounts by unitholders.” A copy of SEBI Circular dated November 08, 2023, is enclosed for your reference and for necessary action at your end. The copy of the circular is also available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com). This is for your information please. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. Yogesh Deshmukh Senior Manager
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued this November 9, 2023 circular to all Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) to notify them of, and require compliance with, SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-RAC-1/P/CIR/2023/178 dated November 8, 2023. The underlying SEBI circular introduces a procedural framework for handling unclaimed amounts held by InvITs and sets out how unitholders may claim those amounts, so the practical compliance impact is on InvITs that hold unpaid/distributable sums that remain unclaimed by beneficiaries.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that this NSE communication is a forwarding/implementation notice: it does not itself create new substantive requirements, but it directs InvITs to follow the SEBI circular and take “necessary action” in line with the new framework. The document does not specify any separate effective date or deadline beyond the SEBI circular date of November 8, 2023 and the NSE circular date of November 9, 2023. No thresholds, rates, or quantitative limits are stated in the NSE notice itself.

Entities affected are all InvITs listed/covered by NSE’s circular. The required action is to review and implement the SEBI-prescribed process for managing unclaimed amounts and for processing unitholder claims under the new procedure, with the SEBI circular serving as the controlling document. The circular also notes that the SEBI text is enclosed and available on the NSE website for reference, indicating that compliance teams should consult the SEBI circular itself for the detailed operational steps and filing/verification requirements.

rows.title: Mandatory Filing of Voting Results in XBRL Mode
rows.desc: Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2023/74 Date: October 17, 2023 The Company Secretary All Listed Entities Subject: Mandatory Filing of Voting Results in XBRL Mode Dear Sir/ Madam, This is in reference to Regulation 44(3) of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 which requires the listed entities to submit the Voting Results within two working days of conclusion of its General Meeting in the format specified by SEBI. Currently, the listed entities are filing the Voting Results of the General Meeting both in the PDF and XBRL format. To facilitate ease of compliance for the listed entities, it has been decided to discontinue the PDF reporting format of the Voting Results submission and continue the filings in the XBRL format only. The prescribed XBRL format for filing the Voting Results is available at the below mentioned path: Path:- NEAPS> Compliance > Event Based Compliances > Voting Result The listed entities are requested to submit voting result disclosure only in XBRL form on the following path: Path:- NEAPS > Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Voting Results It is pertinent to note that the Voting Results shall be filed mandatorily by all the listed entities through the XBRL mode only with effect from November 01, 2023. Further, submission of Voting Results in the XBRL form will only be treated as compliance under Regulation 44(3) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 and no other form of filing (including PDF form) will be treated as compliance. The listed entities are requested to please take note of the above and ensure compliance. In case of any filing related concerns on the captioned subject, please reach out to the Exchange at takeover@nse.co.in and contact details given on NEAPS platform. Yours Faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Pooja Kothari Manager – Listing Compliance
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India Limited issued Circular NSE/CML/2023/74 on October 17, 2023, addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed entities, to change how voting results for general meetings must be filed under Regulation 44(3) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. Under Regulation 44(3), listed entities must submit voting results within two working days of the conclusion of the general meeting in the format specified by SEBI; this circular says NSE is discontinuing the PDF reporting format and will accept only XBRL filings going forward.

The practical compliance change is that all listed entities must file voting result disclosures exclusively through XBRL mode, and the PDF version will no longer count as compliant filing. The prescribed XBRL format is available in NEAPS under Compliance > Event Based Compliances > Voting Result, and the submission path for the required filing is NEAPS > Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > Voting Results. This requirement becomes mandatory for all listed entities with effect from November 1, 2023.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that only an XBRL submission will be treated as satisfying Regulation 44(3); any other form of filing, including PDF, will not be regarded as compliance. Listed entities are instructed to ensure they have moved to the XBRL-only process and to contact the exchange at takeover@nse.co.in, or use the contact details available on the NEAPS platform, if they encounter filing issues.

rows.summary:

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the subject matter is a **centralized process routed through KRAs (KYC Registration Agencies)** for reporting an investor’s death, which would affect listed entities and any related shareholder/investor servicing processes that involve transmission of securities, updating investor records, or handling deceased-investor cases. The NSE notice itself does **not** specify the operational steps, timelines, forms, or thresholds; those details would be contained in the underlying SEBI circular that accompanies it. Based on this notice alone, the only explicit timing information is the **SEBI issuance date of October 3, 2023** and the **NSE forwarding date of October 4, 2023**.

Compliance teams should therefore treat this as a trigger to review the SEBI circular and assess whether internal procedures need to be updated so that any reporting of an investor’s demise is handled through the newly centralized KRA-based mechanism rather than ad hoc processes. rows.title: Revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on application filed under Regulation 37 and 59A of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 w.r.t. Scheme of Arrangements.
rows.desc: Circular Department: LISTING Download Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/70 Date: September 29, 2023 The Company Secretary All Listed Companies Subject: - Revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on application filed under Regulation 37 and 59A of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 w.r.t. Scheme of Arrangements. This has reference to the draft scheme of arrangement filed with stock exchanges under Regulation 37 and 59A of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 read along with SEBI Master Circulars dated June 20, 2023, SEBI operational circular SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div1/P/CIR/2022/0000000103 dated July 29, 2022 updated on December,01 2022 and amendment thereof. In this regard, kindly find below the revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) to be followed by listed entities: 1. The Scheme of Arrangement seeking Stock Exchange’s NOC under Regulation 37 / 59A of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘SEBI LODR’) shall be submitted to the Exchange along with all the documents as per the Exchange Checklist within 15 working days of board meeting approving the draft scheme of arrangement. In case the application is not submitted within 15 working days, the company shall take fresh approval from its board considering fresh financials, valuation report, etc. 2. At the time of submission of the application to the Exchange(s) under Regulation 37 / 59A of SEBI LODR, the Audited Financials of last 3 years (financials not being older than 6 months) of unlisted company(ies) involved in the Scheme of Arrangement has to be submitted as required under para (A) (2) (f) of Part I of SEBI Master Circular dated June 20, 2023 and para (A) (2) (e) of Part I of Chapter XII of SEBI operational Circular SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div1/P/ CIR/2022/0000000103 dated July 29, 2022 updated on December 01, 2022. 3. Audited financials considered for preparation of Valuation Report, should not be older than 3 months on the date of valuation report. While submitting with Exchange, the detailed working of valuation under different methods shall also be given. 4. The board shall consider the scheme of arrangement within 7 working days of the issuance of valuation report. 5. At the time of submission of application with the stock exchange(s) under: i. Regulation 37: Documents referred in para (A) (2) of Part I of SEBI Master Circular dated June 20, 2023 (as amended) as well as included in the checklist of respective stock exchange(s), should be complete in all aspects. ii. Regulation 59A: Documents referred in para (A) (2) of Part I of Chapter XII of SEBI operational Circular SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div1/P/CIR/2022/0000000103 dated July 29, 2022 updated on December,01 2022 as well as included in the checklist of the respective stock exchange(s), should be complete in all aspects. Note: For Listed Entity having their specified securities as well as NCDs/NCRPS listed, a single filing of the draft scheme of arrangement in terms of Regulations 37 and Regulation 59A of SEBI LODR shall be submitted under Regulation 37 wherein additional documents, as required for Debt Listed company shall also be attached. 6. Exchange Queries: - a If the documents (referred in point no.5) are incomplete or any material inadequacies/non- compliance with the SEBI Circulars referred above are observed in the documents, by the Exchange, the scheme shall be returned to the Company for filing the scheme after ensuring compliance. In such cases the processing fee paid by the company will be forfeited by the Exchange/Regulator. b If any clarification is required from the company side, a period of 7 working days from date of raising query by the Exchange will be allowed to the company for submission of rectification. On expiry of aforesaid timelines if the company is unable to make submissions, then any fees paid by the Company for processing of the application shall be forfeited by the Exchange/Regulator and the scheme documents shall be returned to the company. 7. For only Debt Listed Entities: The Listed Entity shall submit their revert to queries (if any) raised by the Stock Exchange as early as possible, to enable adherence to requirement of “maximum number of days for providing the ‘No-Objection’ Letter to SEBI shall not exceed thirty days from the date of receipt of the draft scheme of arrangement”. 8. Any refiling because of the previous unsatisfactory filing shall be made along with a fresh set of documents all together including valuation report, fairness opinion, recommendation of the audit committee, etc. The company shall be required to pay fresh fees to the Exchange/Regulator. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. Dipti Chinchkhede Senior Manager
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated September 29, 2023 revises the standard operating procedure for listed entities filing draft schemes of arrangement with stock exchanges under Regulation 37 and Regulation 59A of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. It applies to listed companies seeking the stock exchange’s no-objection letter/NOC for schemes of arrangement, and it requires submission of the draft scheme with all documents in the relevant exchange checklist within 15 working days of the board meeting approving the draft scheme; if the company misses that 15-working-day window, it must obtain fresh board approval based on fresh financials, valuation reports, and related updated materials. For applications under Regulation 37 or 59A, the listed entity must submit audited financials for the last 3 years of any unlisted company(ies) involved in the scheme, and those financials must not be older than 6 months at the time of filing; separately, the audited financials used for the valuation report must not be older than 3 months as of the valuation report date, and the company must provide detailed workings supporting the valuation under each method used.

The board is required to consider the scheme within 7 working days of issuance of the valuation report. When filing, all documents required under the applicable SEBI circular provisions and the exchange checklist must be complete and compliant: for Regulation 37 filings, the documents listed in para (A)(2) of Part I of the SEBI Master Circular dated June 20, 2023 (as amended) must be fully submitted; for Regulation 59A filings, the documents listed in para (A)(2) of Part I of Chapter XII of the SEBI operational circular dated July 29, 2022, updated on December 1, 2022, must be fully submitted. If an entity has both listed equity securities and listed NCDs/NCRPS, it may make a single filing under Regulation 37, but it must include the additional documents required for a debt-listed company as well.

The circular also tightens the exchange-query process. If the exchange finds missing documents, material inadequacies, or non-compliance with the referenced SEBI circulars, it will return the scheme filing to the company for resubmission after compliance, and any processing fee already paid will be forfeited. If the exchange seeks clarifications, the company gets 7 working days from the date the query is raised to respond; failure to respond within that period will also result in forfeiture of the processing fee and return of the scheme documents. For debt-listed entities specifically, responses to stock exchange queries must be submitted as early as possible so the exchange can meet the requirement that the no-objection letter to SEBI be issued within a maximum of 30 days from receipt of the draft scheme. Finally, any refiling after an unsatisfactory earlier filing must be made as a completely fresh submission with all supporting documents again, including the valuation report, fairness opinion, and audit committee recommendation, and the company must pay fresh fees.

rows.title: Format of Cyber Security Incidence Disclosure under Corporate Governance Report
rows.desc: Non-Confidential To, All Listed Entities, Sub: Format of Cyber Security Incidence Disclosure under Corporate Governance Report 1. Overview SEBI vide Notification No. SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2023/131 dated June 14, 2023 issued SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2023 and inserted sub clause 27(2)(ba) wherein it is specified that the details of Cyber Security incidents or breaches or loss of data or documents shall be disclosed in the Corporate Governance Report and shall be submitted by the listed entities to the stock exchanges on a quarterly basis which is effective from July 14, 2023 onwards. 2. Based on above mentioned requirement and various discussions with SEBI, following new fields have been added to the existing Corporate Governance Report utility: Details of Cyber Security Incidence Whether as per Regulation 27(2)(ba) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 there has been cyber security incidents or breaches or loss of data or documents during the quarter Yes/No Date of the event Brief details of the event The abovementioned changes in the XBRL utility will be effective from the quarter ended September 30, 2023 and onwards. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Raksha Jain Senior Manager
rows.summary:
SEBI has amended the Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015 to require listed entities to disclose cyber security incidents, breaches, or any loss of data or documents in the Corporate Governance Report under new sub-clause 27(2)(ba). This disclosure obligation applies to all listed entities and must be submitted to the stock exchanges on a quarterly basis, with the regulatory requirement effective from July 14, 2023 onward.  

In response, the National Stock Exchange has updated the existing Corporate Governance Report XBRL utility to include new mandatory fields for cyber security incident reporting. The added fields require the listed entity to state whether any cyber security incident, breach, or loss of data/documents occurred during the quarter under Regulation 27(2)(ba) on a Yes/No basis, provide the date of the event, and include brief details of the event.  

The XBRL utility changes will apply starting with the quarter ended September 30, 2023 and for all subsequent quarters. From a compliance perspective, this means listed entities must now track such incidents during each quarter and ensure the relevant disclosure is completed and filed in the quarterly Corporate Governance Report submitted to the stock exchanges.

rows.title: Filing of Related Party Transactions disclosure on NEAPS Portal
rows.desc: Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2023/68 Date: September 29, 2023 The Company Secretary All Listed Entities Subject: Filing of Related Party Transactions disclosure on NEAPS Portal Dear Sir/ Madam, This has reference with Regulation 23(9) of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 which requires the listed entities to submit disclosure of related party transactions (RPT) every six months on the date of publication of its standalone and consolidated financial results and Exchange Circular number NSE/CML/2021/34 dated September 06, 2021 and Circular Ref. rows.summary:

This applies to all listed entities subject to the related party transaction disclosure requirement. The circular references earlier NSE circulars **NSE/CML/2021/34 dated September 6, 2021** and **NSE/CML/2021/42 dated October 19, 2021**, which dealt with XBRL-based filing of RPT disclosures for listed companies at NSE, indicating this is a reaffirmation of the filing method and compliance standard.

Listed entities are expected to ensure their internal filing process routes the RPT disclosure through the XBRL upload workflow on NEAPS at the time of financial results publication, rather than relying on any parallel PDF or alternative filing. rows.title: Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Extending framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level to all listed companies in a phased manner
rows.summary:
The document is a SEBI-related market conduct circular on the trading window closure framework under Clause 4 of Schedule B of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. It extends the existing mechanism that restricts trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at the security level so that it applies to all listed companies, and it does so in a phased manner rather than as an immediate blanket change. The practical effect is that once a trading restriction is triggered for a DP in one listed security, trades in that security can be blocked through PAN-based controls at the market/intermediary level, reducing the risk of circumvention through multiple accounts or intermediaries.

From a compliance perspective, this means listed entities must align their insider-trading controls, DP identification, and trading window closure processes with the expanded PAN-freeze framework. Companies will need to ensure that the list of DPs is accurate and timely, that PAN details are captured correctly for all relevant persons, and that internal procedures for imposing and lifting trading window closures are coordinated with the new security-level freeze process. The document’s title indicates that the framework is being rolled out “to all listed companies in a phased manner,” so compliance teams should expect implementation sequencing, interim readiness obligations, and the need to monitor further operational guidance from the exchange/SEBI ecosystem for exact onboarding timelines and technical procedures.

rows.title: Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Extending framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level to all listed companies in a phased manner
rows.summary:
The document is a SEBI-related circular titled “Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Extending framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level to all listed companies in a phased manner.” Its core change is that listed companies are being moved to a mechanism where trading by Designated Persons is restricted by **freezing the PAN at the security level**, rather than relying only on traditional trading window closure controls. The purpose is to strengthen insider-trading compliance by preventing prohibited trades more effectively across the market infrastructure.

The document extends this PAN-freezing framework to **all listed companies**, but **in a phased manner**, meaning companies will be brought under the requirement according to a SEBI-mandated rollout sequence rather than all at once. It applies to **Designated Persons** under the PIT Regulations and is tied specifically to the trading restrictions contemplated under **Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9** of the PIT Regulations. Compliance teams should therefore treat this as an additional enforcement layer on top of existing insider-trading controls, not merely a clarification of the trading window concept.

From a compliance perspective, the key operational obligation is that companies must ensure that trading by DPs is blocked at the PAN/security level during closure periods or other restricted periods, so that the prohibition is enforced through market systems and not just internal policy. The document does not provide a numeric threshold, rate, or monetary limit; the material requirement is procedural and systems-based. Because the text provided is not readable beyond the title and includes a corrupted file payload, no additional deadlines, cut-off dates, exceptions, or implementation milestones can be reliably extracted from the supplied content. rows.title: Guidance on filing Announcements on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform pursuant to the SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirement) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2023 (“Amended Regulations”)
rows.desc: Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/57 Date: July 14, 2023 The Company Secretary All Listed Entities Subject: Guidance on filing Announcements on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform pursuant to the SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirement) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2023 (“Amended Regulations”) SEBI vide its Notification No. SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2023/131 dated June 14, 2023 further amended the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘SEBI LODR’). The Amended Regulations provides for various amendments and additions in the existing disclosure requirements. In order to bring more transparency and ensure timely disclosure of material events / information by listed entities, SEBI vide its Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/123 dated July 13, 2023 (‘Circular’) has provided further guidance w.r.t the disclosure requirements under Regulation 30 and 30A of SEBI LODR. In view of the above, all listed entities are required to take note of the below key points while filing the disclosure of events/information under Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR: (i) In case of any event emanating from a decision taken in a meeting of board of directors, the listed entities shall: (a) At first file the disclosure in the PDF form under the subject “Outcome of Board Meeting” and shall select “Others” in the Type field in case the event is not mentioned under the existing drop-down options. (b) Mention the Start & End time of the Meeting of the Board of Directors (c) Modify the Announcement Text accordingly specifying the subject of event. (ii) The listed entities shall mandatorily mention the Date & Time of occurrence of the event/information in all the PDF disclosures filed with the Exchange under Regulation 30. (iii) In case of any delayed submission, the listed entity shall ensure that the PDF disclosure filed specifies the reason of delay. The listed entities are requested to take note of the aforementioned disclosure requirements and exercise abundant precaution while filing the disclosure/announcement under Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Pooja Kothari Manager-Listing Compliance
rows.summary:
This NSE circular (Ref. NSE/CML/2023/57 dated July 14, 2023) gives filing instructions for listed entities using the NEAPS platform after SEBI’s June 14, 2023 amendment to the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 and SEBI’s July 13, 2023 guidance circular on Regulations 30 and 30A. The core change is that listed entities must be more precise and standardized when filing material-event disclosures under Regulation 30, especially where the event results from a board meeting decision.

If an event arises from a board of directors meeting, the company must first file the disclosure in PDF format under the subject line “Outcome of Board Meeting.” If the event does not fit an existing NEAPS drop-down category, the filer must select “Others” in the Type field. The company must also include the start and end time of the board meeting and update the announcement text so it clearly states the subject of the event.

For all PDF disclosures filed with the Exchange under Regulation 30, the listed entity must mandatorily state the date and time when the event or information occurred. If the disclosure is delayed, the PDF filing must expressly state the reason for the delay. The circular does not impose a new numerical threshold or rate, but it does create mandatory filing-content requirements that apply to all listed entities making Regulation 30 disclosures, and compliance teams should ensure NEAPS submissions are reviewed carefully before filing to avoid incomplete or non-compliant announcements.

The operational details for implementing the amendments shall be as under: 1. For all the subsequent annual filings of audited financial results, submission of Form A / Form B as the case may be, shall be dispensed with. Consequently, all listed entities shall be required to submit either declaration as mentioned in SEBI Circular CIR/CFD/CMD/56/2016 (in case of audit report with unmodified opinion(s)) or ‘Statement on Impact of Audit Qualifications’ (in case of modified opinion(s)), in the format as specified in Annexure I within the timelines applicable for submission of annual audited financial results. For Audit Qualification(s) where the impact is quantified by the auditor, Management's Views: e. For Audit Qualification(s) where the impact is not quantified by the auditor: (i) Management's estimation on the impact of audit qualification: (ii) If management is unable to estimate the impact, reasons for the same: (iii) Auditors' Comments on (i) or (ii) above: III. Signatories: CEO/Managing Director CFO Audit Committee Chairman Statutory Auditor Place: Date: CHAPTER 11: CIRCULAR ISSUED PERTAINING TO SHAREHOLDING PATTERN, INVESTOR GRIEVANCE REPORT OF SEBI (LISTING OBLIGATIONS AND DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS) REGULATION, 2015 11.1 XBRL based filing of Investor Grievance for Listed Companies at NSE This has a reference with Regulation 13(3) of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, wherein the listed entities are required to file with the recognized stock exchange(s) on a quarterly basis, within twenty-one days from the end of each quarter, a statement giving the number of investor complaints pending at the beginning of the quarter, those received during the quarter, disposed of during the quarter and those remaining unresolved at the end of the quarter. With a view to make the disclosure more accurate and efficient, the Exchange is introducing an offline utility for XBRL filling under Regulation 13(3) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. The Excel Utility for filing the Investor Grievance Report in the prescribed format in XBRL mode has been attached as Annexure 1. Steps for submission of Investor Grievance Report in XBRL mode on NSE’s Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) Portal: 1. Using the Investor Grievance excel utility (attached as Annexure 1), generate XML and follow the steps as mentioned below for submission. 2. Upload XBRL file generated using utility provided as Annexure to this circular in NEAPS a. Go to Compliance > Common XBRL upload > Select option of Investor. Grievance from Modules dropdown and select appropriate quarter. b. Click on upload XBRL file tab. c. Browse and select Xml file to be uploaded. d. On successful upload, “File Uploaded successfully” message would be displayed. e. Acknowledgement mail would be received on the registered email
rows.summary:
This circular package has two main compliance impacts for listed entities. First, it implements the SEBI amendments under Circular No. CIR/CFD/CMD/56/2016 dated May 27, 2016 (with reference to GN/2016-17/001 dated May 25, 2016) on reporting audit qualifications in annual audited financial results. For the financial year ended March 31, 2016, listed entities that already submitted Form A for audit reports with unmodified opinions are deemed to have complied; those that did not submit Form A must file the declaration specified in the SEBI circular, signed by the CEO, Managing Director, CFO, or Audit Committee Chairman, within 30 days from the date of this circular. Separately, all listed entities with modified audit opinions for the year ended March 31, 2016 must submit the “Statement on Impact of Audit Qualifications” in Annexure I within 60 days from the date of this circular, regardless of whether Form B was already filed.

For subsequent annual filings of audited financial results, the requirement to submit Form A or Form B is removed entirely. Going forward, all listed entities must instead submit either the unmodified-opinion declaration (for clean audit reports) or the “Statement on Impact of Audit Qualifications” (for modified opinions), in the Annexure I format, and they must do so within the same timeline that applies to submission of annual audited financial results. Annexure I requires a standalone and consolidated statement showing audited figures and adjusted figures after considering qualifications for turnover/total income, expenditure, net profit/(loss), EPS, total assets, total liabilities, net worth, and any other material financial item the management considers appropriate, followed by a separate narrative for each audit qualification covering the qualification details, type (qualified/disclaimer/adverse), frequency, management’s views, management’s estimated impact if unquantified by the auditor, reasons if the impact cannot be estimated, and the auditor’s comments, with signatures from the CEO/Managing Director, CFO, Audit Committee Chairman, and Statutory Auditor.

The second operational change concerns quarterly investor grievance reporting under Regulation 13(3) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. Listed entities must continue to file, within 21 days from the end of each quarter, the statement of investor complaints pending at the beginning of the quarter, received during the quarter, disposed of during the quarter, and unresolved at quarter-end, but NSE is moving this filing to an XBRL-based process through an offline Excel utility and NEAPS. The utility generates an XML file that must be uploaded via Compliance > Common XBRL upload > Investor Grievance, selecting the relevant quarter; after successful upload, the system displays a success message and sends an acknowledgement email to the registered address.

rows.title: Circular for Seeking comments on XBRL for Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process
rows.desc: Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/41 Date: June 21, 2023 The Company Secretary/Resolution Professional All Listed Companies Subject: Seeking of comments / feedback on the XBRL being introduced for submission of Announcements pertaining to Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (‘CIRP’). 1. OBJECTIVE: The objective of this document is to seek comments / feedback on the proposal to migrate from Portable Document Format (PDF) to eXtensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) format for submitting various corporate announcements for CIRP stages as required under the provisions of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (SEBI LODR), applicable relevant provisions, circulars, guidance note, etc. as amended from time to time. 2. BACKGROUND: Listed entities are required to file the disclosures with the Stock Exchange(s) within prescribed timelines as laid down in SEBI LODR and accordingly it was mandated to report XBRL based filings for financials from year 2015 onwards. With an objective to standardise securities market data it was deliberated that XBRL would be implemented for all corporate filings. Accordingly, Stock Exchanges have implemented XBRL based compliance filing mechanism featuring identical and homogenous compliance data structures which will not only ease the compliance burden on listed entities but also will enable analysis on the data submitted by the listed entities. rows.summary:
This circular, issued by the National Stock Exchange of India on June 21, 2023, is a request for comments from all listed companies and their Company Secretaries/Resolution Professionals on a proposed migration of Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) announcements from PDF to XBRL format. The stated objective is to standardize and streamline disclosure data for CIRP-related announcements under the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 and related SEBI provisions by moving these filings to XBRL exclusively, with the draft format attached as an annexure for feedback on the fields and structure. The exchange explains that it has already been progressively shifting compliance filings from PDF to XBRL, and that this proposal would make CIRP disclosures subject to the same machine-readable reporting approach.

For compliance purposes, the key immediate requirement is not yet a filing mandate, but a consultation response: listed entities may submit suggestions, comments, additions, or modifications to the proposed XBRL fields by email to DL-Announcement@nse.co.in, using the subject line “Comments / Feedback on the XBRL being introduced for CIRP.” The deadline for sending comments is June 25, 2023. The circular provides a detailed draft XBRL schema for CIRP announcements, indicating which fields are mandatory versus non-mandatory and the information expected to be captured, including NSE symbol, company name, BSE scrip code, MSE symbol, ISIN, type of announcement (new/update/revised), type of event, dates of initial/latest/original announcement, and report date.

The draft CIRP event taxonomy is broad and covers multiple stages of the insolvency process: application filed by the company or financial creditors, initiation of CIRP pursuant to an NCLT order, rejection/withdrawal/stay of the application, appointment or replacement of the resolution professional, prior or post-facto intimation of Committee of Creditors meetings, number of resolution plans received, filing of a resolution plan with the tribunal, prior intimation of NCLT consideration of a resolution plan, approval or rejection by the tribunal, liquidation, and an “others” category. For the company-filed CIRP case, the draft also requires the date of the board meeting approving the CIRP event, reasons for opting for CIRP, whether shareholders approved it, the date of the shareholders’ meeting, reasons if shareholder approval was not obtained, details of default in financial obligations as of the date in INR lakhs, whether the default had already been intimated to the exchange under the November 21, 2019 SEBI circular, and the date of the initial default disclosure. The circular also distinguishes between fields intended for public website dissemination and those for exchange-only use, such as certain remarks fields, showing that the proposed XBRL format will require more structured, standardized data capture than current PDF-based narrative filings.
