rows.summary:
This circular is a consultation notice from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited dated June 14, 2023, asking listed entities to comment on a proposal to move certain corporate announcements from PDF submission to mandatory XBRL-only submission. The two announcement categories covered are: (1) loss of share certificate / issue of duplicate share certificate, and (2) closure of trading window, both under SEBI LODR and/or SEBI PIT requirements and any related SEBI law, regulation, circular, or provision. NSE explains that the purpose of the change is to standardize securities market data, reduce compliance burden through a uniform data structure, and improve analysis of disclosures; it also notes that XBRL filings for financials have already been mandated since 2015 and that exchanges have been progressively converting other disclosures from PDF to XBRL.

For the loss/duplicate share certificate item, the draft XBRL format requires very specific data fields, including NSE symbol, company name, BSE scrip code, MSE symbol, ISIN, announcement type (new or revision), event type (loss of share certificates, issue of duplicate share certificates, or “others”), date of original announcement, website remarks, exchange-only remarks, and date of report. It also requires transaction-level details such as the date the company received intimation/information of the lost certificate, shareholder name(s) including joint holders, folio number, number of shares, certificate number, and distinctive number ranges, plus an indication of whether multiple entries must be created for one shareholder and how many entries are needed for that shareholder. The draft further requires identification of the company’s registrar and transfer agent, with a field to specify the name if “Others” is selected, and compliance confirmations on whether the company has complied with Rule 19(3) of the Securities Contract (Regulations) Rules, 1957 and Regulation 39(2) of SEBI LODR; if not compliant, the company must state the reason. The annexure also shows that the loss-of-certificate data structure contemplates add/delete row functionality and a field for the number of shareholders who have reported loss of share certificates.

NSE is specifically soliciting comments, feedback, suggestions, and observations on additions or modifications to the fields in the draft XBRL format, recognizing that the required information is largely descriptive and derived from the existing SEBI framework. Comments must be emailed to DL-Announcement@nse.co.in in a prescribed format that includes the name of the entity/person, contact number and email address, the event category, the subject/heading/field being commented on, comments/suggestions, and detailed rationale. The email subject must read exactly: “Comments / Feedback on the XBRL being introduced for Loss of Share Certificate/ Issue of Duplicate Share Certificate and Closure of Trading Window.” The deadline for submissions is June 20, 2023. The circular does not itself impose the final migration yet; it is a consultation on the draft format, but it clearly signals that listed entities should prepare for exclusive XBRL filing of these announcement types once the format is finalized.

This circular informs all listed entities that the National Stock Exchange will make the facility for filing the Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR) under Regulation 24A of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 available in XBRL mode on the NEAPS platform starting **June 15, 2023**. It is a new filing channel, not a change to the underlying ASCR obligation itself, but it adds a specific technical submission requirement for entities filing through the Exchange.

The circular also sets the filing deadline for the **Secretarial Compliance Report for Financial Year ending March 31, 2023** as **June 30, 2023**. Listed entities subject to Regulation 24A must use the NEAPS workflow to submit the report in XBRL format: log in to the NEAPS portal, navigate to **COMPLIANCE > Common XBRL Upload**, choose **Secretarial Compliance Report** from the Module dropdown, download the offline Excel utility provided for that subject, complete it and generate the XML file, then enter the required portal details, attach the SCR in **PDF** form, and click **“Upload XBRL File”** to finish submission.

The document therefore affects **all listed entities** required to file the ASCR/SCR under SEBI LODR. It does not specify any new numerical thresholds or filing fee changes, but it does impose a specific submission method and sequence for the XBRL filing. For questions, the Exchange directs filers to the Secretarial Compliance team at **nsexbrl@nse.co.in** or via **NEAPS > Help > Contact Us**.

This NSE circular dated May 15, 2023 (Ref. NSE/CML/2023/34) provides FAQs on the use of XBRL format for filing certain equity-related announcements on the NEAPS platform, following the earlier circular NSE/CML/2023/28 dated March 31, 2023. It applies to all listed companies and clarifies that the Exchange is asking companies to file **both** a PDF disclosure and an XBRL submission for the covered subjects during the current transition period; the Exchange will later issue a separate circular stating the effective date after which XBRL will become the operative compliance filing.  

For now, the compliance timeline is that the **XBRL filing must be submitted within 24 hours of the PDF disclosure**, but the **PDF submission is currently the one counted for compliance purposes**. NSE specifically states that this will change only after a further circular, at which point only XBRL submissions will be treated as compliance. Companies with questions are directed to the NSE Announcements team at **takeover@nse.co.in** or the NEAPS contact details.  

The FAQ confirms the XBRL requirement covers the Regulation 30 disclosures listed in the circular, including: issuance or forfeiture of securities; split or consolidation of shares; buyback of securities; restrictions on transferability of securities; and alterations in the terms or structure of existing securities, including forfeiture, reissue of forfeited securities, alteration of calls, and redemption of securities. It also covers binding agreements not in the ordinary course of business, including shareholder agreements, JV agreements, family settlement agreements that affect management and control of the listed entity, and agreements/treaties/contracts with media companies, along with any revisions, amendments, or terminations of those agreements. In addition, it covers fraud/defaults by a promoter, key managerial personnel, or the listed entity itself; arrest of a promoter or KMP; one-time settlements with banks; resolution plans or restructuring relating to bank/financial institution borrowings including inter-creditor arrangements and corporate debt restructuring; and notices of shareholders’ meetings.  

The document further breaks down the covered securities-related events into NEAPS XBRL utility categories, including “Issuance/Allotment/Alteration/Restriction on transferability of securities,” with sub-coverage for issuance of securities under point 2.1 of the September 9, 2015 Continuous Disclosure Requirements Circular, alteration of capital under point 2.2, actions resulting in alteration of the terms or structure of existing securities under point 2.5, restrictions on transferability under point 2.4, and allotment of securities after issuance. The allotment category explicitly includes allotments of equity, preference, convertible, non-convertible, ESOP/ESPS, or other securities, and the FAQ notes that companies may be asked to provide details such as the board meeting date approving the issuance and whether any prior disclosure was made regarding the issuance.

rows.summary:
This circular from the National Stock Exchange of India dated April 10, 2023 is a guidance-only FAQ document for listed entities filing the quarterly Corporate Governance Report on the NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) / data entry / XBRL utility. It does not amend law, SEBI regulations, or prior exchange circulars, but it does set out the Exchange’s required approach for completing specific fields in the submission, and listed entities are instructed to follow it accordingly.

For the Board composition section, if a director does not have a DIN or PAN, the company must enter the prescribed dummy values only — DIN `99999999` and PAN `ZZZZZ9999Z` — and explain the reason in the company remarks. The report must show the director’s correct and complete name as per PAN; if the name or PAN is inconsistent, the Exchange may seek clarification or issue an advisory letter. For chairperson classification, where the chairperson is the promoter or is related to the promoter and is also an Executive Director or Non-Executive Director, the company must select Code `C` together with Code `ED/NED`; where the chairperson is not related to promoters and is also an Executive Director or Non-Executive Director, the company must select Code `C` and Code `ED/NED` as well.

The circular also standardizes how appointment and re-appointment dates are to be entered. For Independent Directors, the initial appointment date is the start of the first term after the Companies Act, 2013 took effect, and the re-appointment date is the start of the second term; the FAQ gives the example that if a person served from 2011, was treated as an Independent Director from 2014, and was re-appointed in 2019, then 2014 is the initial appointment date and 2019 is the re-appointment date. For directors other than Independent Directors, the initial appointment date is the original date they were inducted onto the board, and re-appointment means the date of the current term.

The re-appointment field is mandatory for Independent Directors; if the first term is still continuing and the director has not yet been re-appointed, the company must repeat the initial appointment date in the re-appointment field. The cessation date field is mandatory only when the director’s tenure has ended because of death, resignation, removal, or completion of term, and if a director has died, the reason must be stated in the remarks column. Tenure details are mandatory only for Independent Directors, and the tenure is to be computed up to the end of the current/approved term as applicable.

rows.summary:
The NSE’s April 10, 2023 circular revises the Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR) format for all listed entities by replacing item 1 in the earlier March 16, 2023 circular and adding a new set of mandatory affirmations to be made by the Practicing Company Secretary (PCS). The revised ASCR now requires the PCS to specifically state whether the listed entity complies with applicable Secretarial Standards issued by the ICSI, whether all applicable SEBI-regulatory policies have been adopted with board approval and are kept aligned with SEBI regulations/circulars/guidelines through timely review and updating, whether the company maintains a functional website and timely posts required information in a separate section, and whether web-links cited in the annual corporate governance report under Regulation 27(2) are accurate and directly point to the relevant document or section. It also requires affirmations that none of the company’s directors are disqualified under Section 164 of the Companies Act, 2013; that the listed entity has properly identified material subsidiaries and complied with disclosure requirements for both material and other subsidiaries; that records are preserved and destroyed in accordance with SEBI-prescribed record retention and archival policies under the SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015; that board, independent director, and committee performance evaluations have been carried out at the start of every financial year as required; that all related party transactions received prior Audit Committee approval or, if not, are fully explained and identified as later approved/ratified/rejected; that all Regulation 30 and Schedule III disclosures have been made within the prescribed timelines; and that the entity complies with Regulation 3(5) and 3(6) of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. The PCS must also state whether any action has been taken by SEBI or any stock exchange against the listed entity, its promoters, directors, or subsidiaries, including actions under SEBI’s SOP frameworks, and whether any additional non-compliances have been observed under any SEBI regulation, circular, or guidance note; if any item is marked “No” or “NA,” PCS remarks are mandatory.  

In addition, the circular changes the filing procedure temporarily: although listed entities are currently submitting ASCR in both PDF and XBRL, the XBRL filing mode is still under development, so ASCR must provisionally be submitted in PDF format through the NEAPS announcement path (NEAPS > Compliance > Announcements > Announcements/Corporate Actions Later). NSE states that once the XBRL system is ready, submission in XBRL will also become mandatory. The circular says the rest of the March 16, 2023 requirements remain unchanged, and the revised ASCR format is attached as Annexure A.

rows.summary:
The NSE has expanded the use of XBRL for certain equity-related corporate announcements filed by listed companies on the NEAPS platform. Effective **April 1, 2023**, the following **Regulation 30, SEBI LODR** announcement categories must be made available in **XBRL format**: disclosures relating to issuance or forfeiture of securities, split or consolidation of shares, buyback of securities, restrictions on transferability or changes in the terms/structure of existing securities (including forfeiture, reissue of forfeited securities, alteration of calls, redemption, etc.); binding agreements not in the ordinary course of business (including shareholder agreements, JV agreements, family settlement agreements to the extent they affect management/control, and agreements/treaties/contracts with media companies), including amendments and terminations; fraud/defaults by a promoter, KMP, or the listed entity, or arrest of a promoter/KMP; one-time settlements with banks; resolution plans/restructuring for bank or financial institution borrowings (including inter-creditor arrangements); corporate debt restructuring; and notices of shareholders’ meetings.

For the initial phase, the NSE will still accept the **PDF filing** as compliance with Regulation 30, but listed entities must also file the **XBRL version within 24 hours of the PDF submission**. The circular states that at a later date—**to be announced separately**—the Exchange will move to **XBRL-only submission** for these subjects, so companies should treat the XBRL workflow as mandatory and prepare for a future hard transition away from PDF support.

The filing process must be done through the **NEAPS portal** at **https://neaps.nseindia.com/NEWLISTINGCORP** by navigating to **COMPLIANCE → Common XBRL Upload → Equity Announcement-XBRL**, selecting the relevant announcement subject, downloading the appropriate offline Excel utility, completing it to generate an XML file, and then uploading that XML file on the portal along with the required details. If companies have questions, they are directed to contact the NSE Announcements team at **takeover@nse.co.in** or use the contact details available on NEAPS.

rows.title: Extension of compliance period – Fund raising by large corporates through issuance of debt securities to the extent of 25% of their incremental borrowings in a financial year
rows.desc: Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No: NSE/CML/2023/27 Date: March 31, 2023 The Company Secretary All Listed Companies Subject: Extension of compliance period – Fund raising by large corporates through issuance of debt securities to the extent of 25% of their incremental borrowings in a financial year Dear Sir/ Madam, This is with reference to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHSRACPOD1/P/CIR/2023/049 dated March 31,2023 issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) titled “Extension of compliance period – Fund raising by large corporates through issuance of debt securities to the extent of 25% of their incremental borrowings in a financial year”. A copy of SEBI Circular dated March 31, 2023 is enclosed for your reference and for necessary action at your end. The copy of the circular is also available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com). This is for your information please. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. Sandeep Dhamal Manager
rows.summary:
This NSE circular merely forwards and references SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHSRACPOD1/P/CIR/2023/049 dated March 31, 2023, and states that it is being issued for information and necessary action by listed companies. The subject of the SEBI circular is an **extension of the compliance period** for the requirement applicable to **large corporates** to **raise funds through issuance of debt securities to the extent of 25% of their incremental borrowings in a financial year**. The document itself does not set out the new extended deadline or the detailed mechanics; it directs recipients to the attached SEBI circular and to the NSE website for the operative text.

From a compliance perspective, the key point is that this is **not a new substantive funding obligation**, but an **extension of time to comply** with an existing framework concerning debt fundraising by large corporates. The affected entities are **listed companies** that fall within the SEBI definition of **large corporates** under the incremental borrowing/debt issuance regime. Compliance officers should review the underlying SEBI circular to confirm the revised compliance period, any reporting or disclosure deadlines, and whether any internal financing plans or debt issuance schedules need to be updated to align with the extended timeline.

rows.title: Introduction of Issue Summary Document (ISD) – Further Issues
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Download Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/26 Date: March 31, 2023 To All Listed Entities, Sub: Introduction of Issue Summary Document (ISD) – Further Issues Dear Sir/Madam, This circular is in reference with SEBI circular SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/29 dated February 15, 2023 in relation to Introduction of Issue Summary Document (ISD) and dissemination of issue advertisements. The said circular has introduced ISD for the following Further Issues, in XBRL (Extensible Business Reporting Language) format, effective from April 03, 2023: • Preferential issue, • Qualified institutions placement (QIP), • Rights issue, • Issue of American Depository Receipts (ADR), • Issue of Global Depository Receipts (GDR) and • Issue of Foreign Currency Convertible Bonds (FCCBs) Accordingly, the Stock Exchanges have develop a utility in order to facilitate the filing of the ISD by the listed entities. Said utilities are attached herewith as Annexure A. Submission of details as per the ISD shall be mandatory for all the following application being submitted on or after April 03, 2023: • Applications obtaining in-principle approval under reg 28(1) of SEBI (LODR) regulations, 2015 • Applications obtaining in-principle listing approval post the allotment of securities The listed entities shall submit the details, to any stock exchange where the securities of the entity, in relation to which the ISD is being filed, are listed. If the details are being submitted with NSE, the same shall be submitted in the manner mentioned in Annexure B. National Stock Exchange of India You are requested to take a note of above directions and comply accordingly. Non-adherence to the above directions shall be treated as non-compliance and the respective application may not be approved. In case of any queries pertaining to the said circular please feel free to write us on dl-fi@nse.co.in. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Charmi Dharod Senior Manager
rows.summary:
This NSE circular requires listed entities to begin filing a new Issue Summary Document (ISD) in XBRL format for specified “Further Issues,” pursuant to SEBI circular SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/29 dated February 15, 2023. The ISD requirement applies to preferential issues, qualified institutions placements (QIP), rights issues, issuances of American Depository Receipts (ADR), Global Depository Receipts (GDR), and Foreign Currency Convertible Bonds (FCCBs), with the new framework effective from April 3, 2023. NSE notes that stock exchanges have developed a utility to support filing, and the filing utility/instructions are provided in Annexure A, with NSE-specific submission procedure set out in Annexure B.

For compliance purposes, submission of ISD details is mandatory for any application filed on or after April 3, 2023 that seeks either: (i) in-principle approval under Regulation 28(1) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, or (ii) in-principle listing approval after allotment of securities. The listed entity must submit the ISD details to any stock exchange where the relevant securities are listed; if submitting to NSE, the filing must follow the method prescribed in Annexure B. The circular warns that failure to follow these directions will be treated as non-compliance and the corresponding application may not be approved.

rows.title: Standard Operating Process under SEBI(PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (“SDD”)
rows.desc: Department: Listing Circular Ref. No: NSE/CML/25 Date: March 29, 2023 To All Listed Entities, Sub: Standard Operating Process under SEBI(PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (“SDD”) This is in continuation to the circular No. NSE/CML/2022/51, circular No. NSE/CML/2022/52 dated November 04, 2022, Circular No. NSE/CML/2023/09 dated January 25, 2023 and circular Ref No: NSE/CML/ 2023/21 dated March 16, 2023 issued by the Exchange, the listed entities are advised to take a note that the listed entities to whom the provisions of Regulation 24A of SEBI(LODR) Regulations, 2015 are not applicable, are required to continue to submit SDD Compliance certificate on quarterly basis within 21 days from end of each quarter on sdd_pit@nse.co.in email id. The circular shall be effective immediately. All Listed companies are requested to take note and comply accordingly. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Yogesh Deshmukh Senior Manager
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated March 29, 2023 reiterates and continues the requirement for listed entities that are **not subject to Regulation 24A of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015** to maintain compliance with the **Structured Digital Database (SDD)** requirements under **SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015**. The key instruction is that such listed entities must **continue to submit the SDD Compliance Certificate on a quarterly basis**.

The filing deadline is **within 21 days from the end of each quarter**, and the certificate must be submitted by email to **sdd_pit@nse.co.in**. The circular expressly states that it is in continuation of prior NSE circulars dated **November 4, 2022**, **January 25, 2023**, and **March 16, 2023**, indicating that this is a continuing compliance obligation rather than a new substantive rule change.

The circular applies to **all listed entities**, but the specific quarterly certificate requirement is directed at those for whom **Regulation 24A of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 is not applicable**. The circular is **effective immediately**, so compliance teams should ensure ongoing quarterly tracking and timely submission without waiting for any further implementation date.

rows.title: Review of Securities available for trading under “permitted to trade” category
rows.desc: Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/24 Date: March 29, 2023 To All Members and All Permitted to trade Companies, Subject: Review of Securities available for trading under “permitted to trade” category. Dealing in Securities are permitted on the Exchange as provided in Chapter IV - 2 (c) of the Byelaws and 3.1.1 of the Regulations - Part A (Capital Market Segment) of the Exchange. Based on the above provision the Exchange has been admitting companies for dealings on NSE as “Permitted to Trade”. Chapter IV – Section 12 of the Byelaws and 3.1.2 of the Regulations - Part A (Capital Market Segment) Exchange has a provision that Exchange may prohibit dealings in any security and also at its discretion at any time suspend trading in particular securities as it deems fit. Such suspension shall take effect, on such conditions and in such time and manner as the Exchange may prescribe in this regard. The companies admitted for dealing under “Permitted to trade” do not execute the listing agreement with Exchange and therefore do not provide the full disclosures. Based on the feedback received from the stakeholders, a need was felt to review the process for “permitted to trade” category and accordingly the permitted to trade companies are being reviewed in consultation with and on the advice of the Relevant Authority of the Exchange. The decisions of the authority shall be informed to the market participants and adequate notice shall be provided before withdrawing the scrip from “permitted to trade” category. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Avishkar Naik Head – Listing Compliance
rows.summary:
This circular announces that the National Stock Exchange of India Limited is reviewing securities currently admitted for trading under the “permitted to trade” category. It explains that trading in securities under this category is allowed under Chapter IV-2(c) of the Byelaws and Regulation 3.1.1 of Part A of the Capital Market Segment, and that NSE has been admitting companies for dealings on this basis. The Exchange also notes that, under Chapter IV, Section 12 of the Byelaws and Regulation 3.1.2, it may prohibit dealings in any security and may suspend trading in particular securities at any time, in whatever manner and subject to whatever conditions it prescribes.

The circular highlights a key compliance distinction: companies admitted under “permitted to trade” do not execute the exchange listing agreement and therefore do not provide the full set of disclosures expected of listed entities. Because of stakeholder feedback, NSE is now reviewing the continued use of this category in consultation with, and on the advice of, the Exchange’s Relevant Authority. The document does not itself set a final removal list or immediate trading restriction; instead, it says the authority’s decisions will be communicated to market participants and that adequate notice will be given before any scrip is withdrawn from the “permitted to trade” category.

For compliance teams, the practical point is to monitor whether any securities in this category are subject to withdrawal following the review, and to prepare for a potential change in trading status only after NSE issues formal notice. The circular is dated March 29, 2023 and is addressed to all members and all permitted-to-trade companies.

rows.title: Common and simplified norms for processing investor’s service requests by RTAs and norms for furnishing PAN, KYC details and Nomination
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No: NSE/CML/2023/23 Date: 22 March, 2023 The Company Secretary All Listed Companies Subject: Common and simplified norms for processing investor’s service requests by RTAs and norms for furnishing PAN, KYC details and Nomination Dear Sir/ Madam, This is with reference to SEBI circular no. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/37 dated March 16, 2023 issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) titled “Common and simplified norms for processing investor’s service requests by RTAs and norms for furnishing PAN, KYC details and Nomination”. A copy of SEBI circular dated March 16, 2023 is enclosed for your reference and for necessary action at your end. The copy of the circular is also available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com). This is for your information please. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. Yogesh Deshmukh Senior Manager
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a forwarding notice to all listed companies about a SEBI circular dated 16 March 2023 titled “Common and simplified norms for processing investor’s service requests by RTAs and norms for furnishing PAN, KYC details and Nomination.” NSE’s own communication is dated 22 March 2023 and does not itself introduce substantive requirements; it advises that the SEBI circular is enclosed and should be acted on as necessary.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the subject matter concerns how registrars and transfer agents (RTAs) must process investor service requests, and the norms applicable to furnishing PAN, KYC details, and nomination information. The NSE notice does not reproduce the operative SEBI requirements, deadlines, thresholds, or procedural steps in the text provided, so the underlying obligations would need to be taken directly from the SEBI circular referenced above. The notice indicates that the SEBI circular is available through NSE and is intended for information and necessary action by listed companies, implying that issuer-side coordination with RTAs and investor-facing compliance processes may be affected.

Because this NSE document is only a cover communication, it does not specify any separate effective date, grace period, reporting timeline, or numerical thresholds of its own beyond the SEBI circular’s date of 16 March 2023. A compliance team should treat this as a prompt to review the SEBI circular in full and confirm any changes required in issuer/RTA workflows relating to PAN, KYC, and nomination documentation for shareholders.

rows.title: Path of filing of disclosures related to Corporate Action on NEAPS Portal
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: LISTING Download Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/22 Date: March 21, 2023 The Company Secretary All Listed Companies Dear Sir / Madam, Sub: Path of filing of disclosures related to Corporate Action on NEAPS Portal Please refer Regulation 10 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 which requires all listed entities to file all reports, statements, documents, filings, and any other information to the Exchange on the specified electronic platform. The Exchange has designated NEAPS Portal as the specified electronic platform for filings at National Stock Exchange of India Limited. It is observed that certain listed entities are uploading the disclosure of corporate action (e.g., Record Date or Book Closure dates for Dividend, Annual General Meeting, etc.) in announcements under subjects like Outcome of the Board /Shareholder Meeting, etc. The listed entities are requested that the intimation regarding fixation of Record Date or Book Closure Dates for any corporate action, needs to be separately intimated to the Exchange. Please note a separate tab for Corporate Actions is available on the NEAPS Portal (i.e., NEAPS – Compliance – Announcements - Announcements/CA - Intimation Type: Corporate Action). Thus, all intimation regarding Record Date or Book Closure Dates for any Corporate Action is to be filed separately under this tab. Please note that non-intimation of Record Date or Book Closure Dates separately under Regulation 42 may result in the Exchange not taking the same on record and listed entities will be responsible for subsequent consequences. It is reiterated that the Exchange will take cognizance of only those disclosures which are filed under relevant path as specified above using NSE’s Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS). Listed entities are requested to please take note of the above and ensure compliance. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Yogesh Deshmukh Senior Manager
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has clarified the required filing path for corporate action disclosures on the NEAPS portal, applicable to all listed companies. Under Regulation 10 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, listed entities must file reports, statements, documents, filings, and other information on the Exchange’s specified electronic platform, and NSE has designated NEAPS for this purpose. The circular states that companies have been incorrectly uploading Record Date or Book Closure Date disclosures for corporate actions such as dividends and annual general meetings within other announcement categories, such as “Outcome of Board/Shareholder Meeting,” and instructs that these intimation(s) must instead be filed separately.

For compliance, all notices fixing a Record Date or Book Closure Date for any corporate action must be submitted through the dedicated NEAPS path: **NEAPS – Compliance – Announcements – Announcements/CA – Intimation Type: Corporate Action**. NSE specifically says it will recognize only disclosures filed under the relevant prescribed path and will take cognizance only of those submissions made through NEAPS in the correct category. The circular emphasizes that separate filing is required under **Regulation 42** for Record Date/Book Closure Date intimation, and failure to do so may result in the Exchange not taking the filing on record, with the listed entity bearing any resulting consequences.

There is no new numerical threshold, rate, or fixed deadline date in the circular; the requirement is immediate and procedural, and it applies to any listed entity making a corporate action disclosure involving Record Date or Book Closure Date. Compliance teams should ensure internal filing controls direct these disclosures to the standalone Corporate Actions tab rather than embedding them in general announcement filings.

rows.title: Additional affirmations by Practicing Company Secretaries (PCS) in Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR)
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/ 2023/21 Date: March 16, 2023 To, All Listed Entities, Sub: Additional affirmations by Practicing Company Secretaries (PCS) in Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR) 1. Overview SEBI vide circular no. CIR/CFD/CMD1/27/2019 dated February 08, 2019 issued the format of Annual secretarial compliance report for listed entities and their material subsidiaries which was effective from March 31, 2019 onwards. The Annual secretarial compliance report to be filed on annual basis by PCS confirming the compliances of all SEBI Regulations, circulars and guidelines. 2. Based on various discussions with SEBI, following are the additional affirmations to be provided while submitting ASCR Sr. No. Particulars Compliance status (Yes/No/NA) Observations /Remarks by PCS* 1. Secretarial Standard The compliances of listed entities are in accordance with the Auditing Standards issued by ICSI, namely CSAS-1 to CSAS-3 2. Adoption and timely updation of the Policies: • All applicable policies under SEBI Regulations are adopted with the approval of board of directors of the listed entities National Stock Exchange of India • All the policies are in conformity with SEBI Regulations and has been reviewed & timely updated as per the regulations/circulars/guidelines issued by SEBI 3. Maintenance and disclosures on Website: • The Listed entity is maintaining a functional website • Timely dissemination of the documents/ information under a separate section on the website • Web-links provided in annual corporate governance reports under Regulation 27(2) are accurate and specific which re- directs to the relevant document(s)/ section of the website 4. Disqualification of Director: None of the Director of the Company are disqualified under Section 164 of Companies Act, 2013 5. To examine details related to Subsidiaries of listed entities: (a) Identification of material subsidiary companies (b) Requirements with respect to disclosure of material as well as other subsidiaries 6. Preservation of Documents: The listed entity is preserving and maintaining records as prescribed under SEBI Regulations and disposal of records as per Policy of Preservation of Documents and Archival policy prescribed under SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015 7. Performance Evaluation: The listed entity has conducted performance evaluation of the Board, Independent Directors and the Committees at the start of every financial year as prescribed in SEBI Regulations 8. Related Party Transactions: (a) The listed entity has obtained prior approval of Audit Committee for all Related party transactions National Stock Exchange of India (b) In case no prior approval obtained, the listed entity shall provide detailed reasons along with confirmation whether the transactions were subsequently approved/ratified/rejected by the Audit committee 9. Disclosure of events or information: The listed entity has provided all the required disclosure(s) under Regulation 30 alongwith Schedule III of SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015 within the time limits prescribed thereunder. 10. Prohibition of Insider Trading: The listed entity is in compliance with Regulation 3(5) & 3(6) SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 11. Actions taken by SEBI or Stock Exchange(s), if any: No Actions taken against the listed entity/ its promoters/ directors/ subsidiaries either by SEBI or by Stock Exchanges (including under the Standard Operating Procedures issued by SEBI through various circulars) under SEBI Regulations and circulars/ guidelines issued thereunder 12. Additional Non-compliances, if any: No any additional non-compliance observed for all SEBI regulation/circular/guidance note etc. *Observations/Remarks by PCS are mandatory if the Compliance status is provided as ‘No’ or ‘NA’ 3. Revised Format of Annual Secretarial Compliance Report: Additional columns have been inserted in the format of ASCR which is provided below: (a) The listed entity has complied with the provisions of the above Regulations and circulars/ guidelines issued thereunder, except in respect of matters specified below: - National Stock Exchange of India Sr . N o. Compliance Requirement (Regulations/ circulars/guid elines including specific clause) Regul ation/ Circul ar No. Deviati ons Action Taken by Type of Action Detai ls of Viola tion Fine Amoun t Observati ons/Rem arks of the Practicin g Company Secretary Manag ement Respon se Remar ks Advisory/Clar ification/Fine /Show Cause Notice/ Warning, etc. (b) The listed entity has taken the following actions to comply with the observations made in previous reports: Sr . N o. Compliance Requirement (Regulations/ circulars/guid elines including specific clause) Regul ation/ Circul ar No. Deviati ons Action Taken by Type of Action Detai ls of Viola tion Fine Amoun t Observati ons/Rem arks of the Practicin g Company Secretary Manag ement Respon se Remarks Advisory/Clar ification/Fine /Show Cause Notice
rows.summary:
NSE’s March 16, 2023 circular (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2023/21) requires all listed entities to use a revised Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR) format that adds several mandatory affirmations by the Practicing Company Secretary (PCS). The original ASCR framework was introduced by SEBI’s February 8, 2019 circular and has been applicable since March 31, 2019; the report remains an annual filing and is used to confirm compliance with SEBI regulations, circulars, and guidelines for listed entities and their material subsidiaries.

The circular expands the PCS’s scope of verification by requiring explicit confirmation on 12 areas: compliance with ICSI Auditing Standards CSAS-1 to CSAS-3; adoption, board approval, and timely updating of all applicable SEBI policies; maintenance of a functional website and timely uploading of required documents/information, including accurate and specific web-links in Regulation 27(2) corporate governance reports; confirmation that none of the company’s directors are disqualified under Section 164 of the Companies Act, 2013; identification and disclosure compliance for material and other subsidiaries; preservation and archival of records as required under SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015; performance evaluation of the Board, Independent Directors, and committees at the start of every financial year; prior Audit Committee approval for all related party transactions, or else detailed reasons plus whether later approved/ratified/rejected; timely disclosure of Regulation 30/Schedule III events and information; compliance with PIT Regulations 3(5) and 3(6); confirmation that neither SEBI nor stock exchanges have taken action against the listed entity, its promoters, directors, or subsidiaries (including under SEBI’s SOPs); and confirmation that no additional SEBI-related non-compliances were observed.

The revised ASCR format also adds two new disclosure tables that must be completed when there are exceptions or follow-up actions. The first table is for cases where the listed entity has not complied with a requirement; it requires the compliance requirement, regulation/circular number, nature of deviation, action taken by the entity, type of action (for example advisory, clarification, fine, show-cause notice, warning), details of the violation, fine amount, PCS observations/remarks, management response, and remarks. The second table is for tracking how the entity has acted on observations from previous reports, and it uses the same fields so that remediation and repeat issues can be monitored. The circular makes clear that PCS observations/remarks are mandatory whenever the compliance status is marked “No” or “NA,” so the revised ASCR is not just a yes/no certification but a more detailed exception-and-remediation reporting exercise.

rows.title: Manner of filing financial results as required under regulation 33 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No: NSE/CML/2023/20 Date: 15 March, 2023 The Company Secretary All Listed Companies, Subject: Manner of filing financial results as required under regulation 33 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 Dear Sir/Madam, This has reference to outcome of board meeting, held to consider and approve financial results, filed by companies under regulation 33 of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. This is to bring to your notice that the Exchange has observed that few companies include shareholders letter, investors presentation in the outcome of board meeting held to consider and approve financial results in which financial results, auditor’s report, etc., as required under the aforementioned regulation, were included much after the said letter, presentation. In this regard, listed entities are requested to note that the PDF of outcome of board meeting held to consider and approve financial results must only include financial results, Auditor’s report and other statements as prescribed under Regulation 33, Part A of Schedule IV of the regulation and related circulars. If the company wishes to disclose any other information such as shareholders letter, investors presentation, it must be done as a separate announcement. The companies are requested to take note of the aforementioned provisions/advisory and exercise abundant precaution while filing the financial results. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. Yogesh Deshmukh Senior Manager
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India’s 15 March 2023 circular clarifies the filing format for listed entities submitting financial results under Regulation 33 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015. The Exchange observed that some companies were filing their “outcome of board meeting” PDF with extra materials such as shareholders’ letters or investor presentations, while the actual financial results, auditor’s report, and other required statements appeared later in the document. NSE is now expressly directing listed entities that the PDF filed as the outcome of the board meeting approving financial results must contain only the financial results, the auditor’s report, and the other documents/statements specifically required under Regulation 33, Part A of Schedule IV, and related circulars.

Any additional disclosures, such as a shareholders’ letter or investor presentation, cannot be embedded in the same financial-results filing and must instead be made through a separate announcement. The circular does not introduce a new substantive reporting deadline or numerical threshold, but it does impose a filing-structure compliance requirement effective immediately upon issuance of the circular, and companies are cautioned to exercise “abundant precaution” when filing under Regulation 33. This applies to all listed companies filing financial results with the Exchange.

rows.title: Operational Guidance - Amendment to Securities and Exchange Board of India (Buy-back of Securities) Regulations, 2018 (“Buy-back Regulations”)
rows.desc: Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No: NSE/CML/2023/19 Date: 09 March, 2023 The Company Secretary All Listed Companies Subject: Operational Guidance -Amendment to Securities and Exchange Board of India (Buy-back of Securities) Regulations, 2018(“Buy-back Regulations”) Dear Sir/ Madam, This is with reference to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/35 dated March 08,2023 issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) titled “Operational Guidance -Amendment to Securities and Exchange Board of India (Buy-back of Securities) Regulations, 2018(“Buy-back Regulations”)” A copy of SEBI Circular dated March 08, 2023 is enclosed for your reference and for necessary action at your end. The copy of the circular is also available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com). This is for your information please. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. Sandeep Dhamal Manager
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated 09 March 2023 is an administrative forwarding notice to all listed companies, directing attention to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/35 dated 08 March 2023, which provides “Operational Guidance” linked to amendments to the SEBI (Buy-back of Securities) Regulations, 2018. The NSE document itself does not introduce independent substantive requirements; rather, it informs listed issuers that the SEBI circular is enclosed and available on the NSE website for necessary action.

For a compliance team, the key point is that SEBI has issued operational guidance in connection with the amended buy-back framework, meaning companies considering or undertaking share buy-backs should review the SEBI circular and align their procedures with the updated regulations and implementation guidance. The notice does not specify the underlying regulatory changes, thresholds, timelines, or technical compliance steps in its own text, so those details must be taken from the referenced SEBI circular. No separate effective date is stated in the NSE communication beyond the date of the SEBI circular itself, 08 March 2023.

rows.title: Filing of Related Party Transactions (RPT) and Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) to be made available on the NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System) platform
rows.desc: CIRCULAR Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2023/18 Date: February 24, 2023 To, All Listed Companies Subject: Filing of Related Party Transactions (RPT) and Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report (BRSR) to be made available on the NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System) platform. Dear Sir/ Madam, This is in continuation to Exchange circular number NSE/CML/2022/58 dated December 15, 2022 informing about filing of Equity announcements and Financial Results on the NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System) platform. With reference to the above and to bring all the filings under one single portal, it has been decided that in addition to the above filings on the NEAPS platform, filings for Related Party Transactions (RPT) and Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report (BRSR) will also be made available on the NEAPS platform with effect from February 25, 2023: • Related Party Transactions - XBRL submission: Filing path:- NEAPS > Common XBRL Upload > Related Party Transactions • Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report - XBRL submission: Filing path:- NEAPS > Common XBRL Upload > Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report Contact details of the Exchange Officers for the respective subjects are available on the NEAPS portal and the companies can get in touch with the respective officers for the issues and queries pertaining to filings on the NEAPS platform. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Avishkar Naik Head – Listing Compliance
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has extended its NEAPS single-portal filing framework so that, in addition to equity announcements and financial results, listed companies must also use NEAPS for two more XBRL submissions: Related Party Transactions (RPT) and the Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report (BRSR). This change is set out in NSE/CML/2023/18 dated February 24, 2023, and it takes effect from February 25, 2023.  

From the effective date onward, the filing routes are specifically: **NEAPS > Common XBRL Upload > Related Party Transactions** for RPT, and **NEAPS > Common XBRL Upload > Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report** for BRSR. The circular does not change the substantive reporting content or thresholds for RPT or BRSR; it changes the filing platform/process by requiring these submissions to be made available through NEAPS as part of the Exchange’s effort to consolidate filings under one portal.  

Compliance teams should ensure that personnel responsible for statutory/stock exchange filings are prepared to submit these reports through NEAPS starting on the effective date, and should use the Exchange’s designated officer contacts available on the NEAPS portal for any filing issues or queries. The circular applies to **all listed companies**.

rows.title: Resolution of Company complaints through NEAPS
rows.desc: Circular Department: Investor Services Cell Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/17 Date: February 17, 2023 The Company Secretary All Listed Companies Subject: Resolution of Company complaints through NEAPS Dear Sir/ Madam, The Exchange has been providing a mechanism to resolve complaints pertaining to Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirement (LODR) received from Investors against the ‘Listed Companies’. With a view to provide easy access of complaints registered against the ‘Listed Companies’ vide the common platform, the Exchange has now introduced a new functionality on the NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform, wherein the listed companies can now view all complaints registered against them. The major advantages of this functionality are as under: 1. All complaints received against the ‘Listed Companies’ would reflect under their respective NEAPS login. 2. Companies can provide their responses online, through the portal. 3. Response (including Annexures) can be attached as pdf. 4. Option to download and export reports is made available on NEAPS. User manual has been provided for better guidance. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Manoj Bhatia Manager – ISC User Manual for Resolution of Company Complaints through NEAPS • Login into NEAPS and enter the requisite login credentials. • Investor complaints module is available at Compliance → Disclosures → Investor Complaint Desk. Print screen given below: Screen 1 • The following details are available: ➢ Complaint Number ➢ Symbol ➢ Company Name ➢ Complainant Name ➢ Complaint Date ➢ Pending days ➢ Status of complaint. • The user has the provision to download the list of complaints using the Export CSV option available on the right side of the screen as shown below: Screen 2 • Once user clicks on the “Complaint No.”, the details of the respective complaint along with supporting details shall be available under the tab ‘Complaint Details’. All the communications sent by Exchange shall also be available under this tab, a screen shot of which is given below: Screen 3 Facility to provide response: • While providing a response to the complaint, the user needs to select “Company Response”. In case the Company wants to make any submission with respect to the said compliant, the same can done by clicking on “Update” button. The display for the same are as shown below: Screen 4 Screen 5 • The Company shall upload the file under “Company file attachment” and shall write requisite remarks in the Company Response box and the then click on “Submit” and select “OK” for submission of the requisite response to the Exchange. The display of the said tabs are as given below. Screen 6 Screen 7 • In case no response is received for any complaint, the company shall receive reminder(s) from the Exchange on regular intervals. rows.summary:
This NSE circular, dated February 17, 2023 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2023/17), applies to all listed companies and concerns the handling of investor complaints related to Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR). The Exchange states that it has introduced a new functionality on the NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) so listed companies can now view all complaints lodged against them through their own NEAPS login, rather than only receiving complaints through other exchange communication channels.

Operationally, the investor complaints module is located in NEAPS under Compliance → Disclosures → Investor Complaint Desk. Once logged in, companies can see each complaint’s complaint number, symbol, company name, complainant name, complaint date, number of pending days, and current status. The module also allows companies to export the complaint list in CSV format, and when a complaint number is opened, the full complaint details and supporting information appear under a “Complaint Details” tab, including all communications previously sent by the Exchange.

For responses, the company must use the “Company Response” function and, if making a submission, click “Update.” The company is required to upload its response file under “Company file attachment,” enter the necessary remarks in the Company Response box, then click “Submit” and confirm with “OK” to send the response to the Exchange; attachments may be uploaded as PDF, including annexures. If the company does not respond, the Exchange will issue reminder(s) at regular intervals, and the non-response status will be reflected in the complaint status display.

The circular does not create a new filing deadline for complaints, but it clearly establishes a new compliance workflow: listed companies are expected to monitor complaints in NEAPS, review Exchange communications there, and provide online responses through the portal when required. The Exchange also notes that a user manual is available for guidance, and companies needing assistance may contact the helpline at 18002660050, Option 4.

SEBI has introduced a new compliance requirement for listed entities and issuers that propose to list specified securities: they must file an Issue Summary Document (ISD) in XBRL format, and issue advertisements must be disseminated on the stock exchange’s website. rows.title: FAQ’s on filing of announcements in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform
rows.desc: Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/15 Date: February 07, 2023 The Company Secretary All Listed Companies Subject: FAQ’s on filing of announcements in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform. With reference to the circular dated January 27, 2023, for filing of announcements in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform and further to our demo sessions on the said matter, please find annexed the frequently asked questions (FAQs) for guidance purpose. In case any queries concerning the captioned subject, please reach out to the Announcements team at takeover@nse.co.in or on the contact details given on NEAPS platform. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Dhaval Shah Manager – Listing Encl: Annexure- FAQs ANNEXURE- FAQs 1. Whether listed companies need to file PDF submission also alongwith XBRL submission, if yes, for how long? Yes, both PDF and XBRL submission are required. PDF submission will be required for certain period and subsequently submission in XBRL format exclusively will exist and considered. Exchange will be issuing separate circular for intimating the date for the same. 2. What is the timeline for submitting the disclosure in XBRL format? XBRL filing can be submitted within 24 hours from time of submission of PDF disclosure. 3. From compliance point of view, what will be considered PDF submission or XBRL submission? For certain period, PDF submission will be considered for compliance purpose till PDF submission is accepted, subsequently only XBRL submission will be considered. 4. How to submit disclosure for prior Intimation of Board meeting, which was submitted to Exchange on or before January 28, 2023, and now seeks to add new agenda addition post January 28, 2023? Listed Companies will have to submit the disclosure in PDF and XBRL format for the additional agenda item(s). 5. In case of Outcome of Board Meeting, to which events XBRL submission is applicable? XBRL submission for Outcome of Board meeting will be applicable for Dividend, Buyback, Bonus and Voluntary Delisting events. 6. Whether BSE Limited (BSE) also has same XBRL? Yes, NSE & BSE jointly have developed these XBRL’s utilities, and the XML file generated can be uploaded at both the Exchanges. 7. Are the utilities offline utilities / online utilities? All 4 XBRL utilities are offline utilities. 8. Can we upload BSE XBRL utility on NSE? Yes, XML files generated on BSE can be uploaded on NSE’s portal – NEAPS, similarly the XBRL generated on NEAPS can be uploaded on BSE’s portal. 9. Whether resignation of Company Secretary and Compliance Officer will be through change in KMP, Director RTA etc, XBRL? Yes, for reporting of multiple designations for one person, add multiple rows and respective designation. 10. If the intimation was filed for Board Meeting before the circular however the meeting has been rescheduled, then do we have to file XBRL for rescheduled meeting or PDF? Yes, along with the PDF the XBRL Utility shall also be filed. 11. What if we need to file 2 separate intimations under Reg 29 for same meeting date. For eg: First we filed for financial results and then we wish to file for dividend later on. Under the type of disclosure only 3 options were coming: New, Reschedule or cancel. In case of any new addition in the agenda of the prior intimation which has been already given, it can be given and submitted as a new disclosure. 12. What does new or update mean? New- denotes that the user listed company seeks to submit is providing a new announcement. Update- denotes that the user is providing an update on an earlier announcement submitted. 13. Whether personal information contact details (like PAN/email id/phone number) of KMP/Director/Auditor/RTA etc will be disseminated on NSE Website? No, personal details will not be disseminated on Exchange’s website. 14. In case if company has issue with the macros in utility sheet are disabled. Where to contact? In such cases, Company will have to contact their IT department. 15. What is the difference between original and revision in 4 XBRL? Original- denotes that the user is providing an original announcement Revision- denotes that the user is providing a revision of the earlier announcement submitted. 16. For resignation of statutory auditor, should both change in management XBRL and resignation of statutory auditor XBRL be filed? Yes, for the cases of resignation of Statutory Auditor and Independent Director, firstly the resignation is to be informed and submitted under the general utility and then the specific details of their resignation are to be informed in the respective XBRL utility. 17. Where to submit the disclosure for prior intimation of Board meeting on NEAPS under PDF and XBRL format? Submission of PDF shall be made in Board Meeting module on NEAPS and disclosure in XBRL format shall be uploaded in Common XBRL upload module on NEAPS. NOTE: No PDF submiss
rows.summary:
NSE Circular Ref. No. **NSE/CML/2023/15 dated February 7, 2023** is addressed to all listed companies and serves as guidance on the new process for filing certain stock exchange announcements in **XBRL format on the NEAPS platform**, following the earlier circular of **January 27, 2023** and demo sessions on the subject. The circular does not create a standalone new substantive rule set, but its FAQs clarify how companies must comply during the transition from PDF-only filing to XBRL filing, including that for an initial period **both PDF and XBRL submissions are required**, after which the Exchange will separately notify the date when **XBRL-only filing** will apply and only XBRL will count for compliance. During the transition period, the **PDF submission is the compliance-relevant filing until it is accepted**, and companies must submit the **XBRL version within 24 hours of the PDF disclosure**.

The FAQs specify that if a listed company had already filed a **prior intimation of a Board meeting on or before January 28, 2023**, and later wants to add a new agenda item after that date, it must file the **additional agenda item(s) in both PDF and XBRL**. If a Board meeting already intimated is later **rescheduled**, the company must file **both the PDF and the XBRL utility** for the rescheduled meeting. If the company needs to make **two separate Reg. 29 intimations for the same meeting date**—for example, first for financial results and later for dividend—the later addition is to be treated as a **new disclosure**. For XBRL labeling, **“new”** means a fresh announcement, **“update”** means an update to an earlier announcement, and **“original”** versus **“revision”** similarly distinguish the first filing from a revised one.

The circular also identifies the specific event types for which **Outcome of Board Meeting XBRL filing** applies: **Dividend, Buyback, Bonus, and Voluntary Delisting**. For resignation-related filings, the FAQs state that **resignation of the Company Secretary and Compliance Officer** should be reported using the XBRL utility that allows multiple designations for one person, with **multiple rows** entered for each designation held by that individual. For **resignation of a statutory auditor or an independent director**, the company must first inform the resignation under the **general utility**, and then file the specific resignation details in the **relevant dedicated XBRL utility**. The FAQ also clarifies that personal data such as **PAN, email ID, and phone number** of KMPs, directors, auditors, RTAs, and similar persons **will not be disseminated on the NSE website**.

Operationally, the FAQ confirms that **NSE and BSE jointly developed the XBRL utilities**, that the XML file generated from one exchange’s utility **can be uploaded on the other exchange’s portal**, and that **all four XBRL utilities are offline utilities**. For submissions, the **PDF** for a Board meeting prior intimation must be uploaded in the **Board Meeting module on NEAPS**, while the corresponding **XBRL format filing** must be uploaded in the **Common XBRL upload module on NEAPS**. If companies encounter problems with disabled macros in the utility sheet, NSE directs them to contact **their IT department**. Finally, any queries on the subject should be addressed to NSE’s **Announcements team at takeover@nse.co.in** or via the contact details available on the NEAPS platform.

rows.title: Filing of announcements in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform
rows.desc: Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/11 Date: January 27, 2023 The Company Secretary All Listed Companies Subject: Filing of announcements in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform. With reference to the captioned subject various circulars were issued by Exchange(s) for seeking comments/feedback from listed companies on XBRL format(s) for certain type of announcements. Facility for filings of disclosure for following announcements filed under SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (SEBI LODR) will be available in XBRL format with effect from January 28, 2023: (‘effective date’):  Disclosure under Regulation 29 of SEBI LODR: - Prior Intimation of the Board Meeting.  Disclosure under Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR: - Change in directors, key managerial personnel (Managing Director, Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Company Secretary etc.), Auditor, Compliance Officer and Share transfer agent; - Outcome of Board Meeting for Dividend, Buyback, Bonus Issue and decision on voluntary delisting by the listed entity; - Acquisition(s) (including agreement to acquire), Scheme of Arrangement (amalgamation/ merger/ demerger/restructuring), or sale or disposal of any unit(s), division(s) or subsidiary of the listed entity or any other restructuring. Currently, as a part of compliance all listed entities are required to submit the disclosures in PDF mode as per the provisions of Regulation 30 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations. Further, all listed entities would be required to submit the filings in XBRL mode within 24 hours of submission of the said PDF filing. At a later stage (date to be informed separately) Exchange will shift to only XBRL submission. contd... Please refer the below steps/path for submitting the announcements in XBRL format for the above- mentioned subjects: 1. Post logging in the NEAPS portal (https://neaps.nseindia.com/NEWLISTINGCORP) - go to COMPLIANCE >> Common XBRL Upload 2. On the Common XBRL Upload, please select Equity Announcement-XBRL from the drop down under Module: 3. On clicking the Equity Announcement- XBRL, the user shall then select the Subject of the Announcement from the drop down: contd... 4. On selection of the any given subject, the user can download the XBRL utility for the said subject from the table below (“Download Offline Excel Utilities) and fill-in the utility and generate the XML file. 5. Once the XML is generated from the utility, fill-in the required details on the portal and click on the Upload XBRL File and complete the submission. In case any queries concerning the captioned subject, please reach out to the Announcements team at takeover@nse.co.in or on the contact details given on NEAPS platform. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Dhaval Shah Manager – Listing
rows.summary:
NSE has announced that, effective **January 28, 2023**, listed companies can begin filing certain **SEBI LODR** disclosures in **XBRL format** on the **NEAPS** portal, specifically through **COMPLIANCE >> Common XBRL Upload >> Equity Announcement-XBRL**. The initial announcements covered are: **Regulation 29 prior intimation of a Board meeting**; and under **Regulation 30**, disclosures relating to **changes in directors, key managerial personnel (MD, CEO, CFO, Company Secretary, etc.), auditor, compliance officer, or share transfer agent**; **outcomes of Board meetings for dividend, buyback, bonus issue, or voluntary delisting**; and **acquisition(s), schemes of arrangement (including amalgamation/merger/demerger/restructuring), or sale/disposal of any unit, division, subsidiary, or other restructuring**.

For now, companies must still make the disclosure in **PDF mode** as currently required under Regulation 30, but NSE is adding an additional obligation to file the **same disclosure in XBRL within 24 hours of the PDF submission**. NSE also states that this is an interim arrangement: at a later date, to be communicated separately, the exchange will move to **XBRL-only submission** for these announcements. Compliance teams should therefore treat the PDF filing as the immediate disclosure obligation and the XBRL upload as a mandatory follow-on filing within the 24-hour window.

The filing process requires the user to log in to **https://neaps.nseindia.com/NEWLISTINGCORP**, navigate to the common XBRL upload section, choose the relevant announcement subject, download the applicable **offline Excel XBRL utility**, complete it, generate the **XML file**, and then upload that XML on the portal after entering the required details. Questions are to be directed to NSE’s Announcements team at **takeover@nse.co.in** or via the contact details shown on NEAPS.

rows.title: Standard Operating Process under SEBI(PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (“SDD”)
rows.desc: To All Listed Entities, Sub : Standard Operating Process under SEBI(PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (“SDD”) This is with reference to Regulation 3(5) and 3(6) of SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 which inter alia required SDD to be maintained by the company. In this regard, the Exchange has issued following circulars inter alia Specifying timelines for submission of SDD Compliance certificate and action to be taken against companies which are found to be non-complaint with above mentioned Regulations: 1) Circular No. NSE/CML/2022/51 dated October 28, 2022 specifying timelines for submission of SDD Compliance Certificate for the quarter ended September 30, 2022 and December 31, 2022. 2) Circular No. NSE/CML/2022/52 dated November 04, 2022 specifying consequences of non- compliance with the requirements of Reg 3(5) and 3(6) specifies consequences of non-compliance with the requirements of Reg 3(5) and 3(6) of SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015. In addition to above mentioned Circulars, the companies are advised to take a note of the following: Exchange circular no. NSE/CML/2022/52 dated November 04, 2022 specifies consequences of non- compliance with Reg 3(5) and 3(6) of SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 states as under: "Under the "Get Quote" page of the Exchange Website of the Listed Entity, wherever listed, would display that the company is non-compliant with SDD, from the next trading day till the Exchanges have satisfactorily verified that the company has completely complied." It is clarified that in addition to above, the details of the compliance officer will also be displayed on the "Get Quote" page of the Exchange website where the above information is disseminated. This circular supersedes the earlier circular issued vide refence number NSE/CML/2023/09 dated January 25, 2023 All Listed companies are requested to take note and comply accordingly. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Yogesh Deshmukh Senior Manager
rows.summary:
This circular reiterates that all listed entities must maintain a Structured Digital Database (“SDD”) under Regulations 3(5) and 3(6) of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, and it is specifically aimed at listed companies that are subject to NSE’s compliance monitoring. It refers to earlier NSE circulars that had already set the timeline for submitting the SDD compliance certificate for the quarters ended September 30, 2022 and December 31, 2022, and another circular dated November 4, 2022 that described the consequences of non-compliance with Regulations 3(5) and 3(6).

The key compliance consequence highlighted here is that if a listed entity is found non-compliant with the SDD requirements, the Exchange will display a non-compliance warning on the company’s “Get Quote” page on the Exchange website starting from the next trading day, and that status will remain visible until the Exchange satisfactorily verifies that the company has fully complied. The circular further clarifies an additional disclosure consequence: the details of the compliance officer will also be displayed on the same “Get Quote” page where this non-compliance information is published.

No new substantive SDD filing deadline or numerical threshold is introduced in this circular itself; rather, it reinforces the existing obligation to maintain SDD records and warns of the Exchange’s public disclosure mechanism for companies that fail to comply. It also states that this circular supersedes NSE circular reference number NSE/CML/2023/09 dated January 25, 2023, and requests all listed companies to take note and comply accordingly.

rows.title: Standard Operating Process under SEBI(PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (“SDD”)
rows.desc: To All Listed Entities, Sub : Standard Operating Process under SEBI(PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (“SDD”) This is with reference to Regulation 3(5) and 3(6) of SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 which inter alia required SDD to be maintained by the company. In this regard, the Exchange has issued following circulars inter alia Specifying timelines for submission of SDD Compliance certificate and action to be taken against companies which are found to be non-complaint with above mentioned Regulations: 1) Circular No. NSE/CML/2022/51 dated October 28, 2022 specifying timelines for submission of SDD Compliance Certificate for the quarter ended September 30, 2022 and December 31, 2022. 2) Circular No. NSE/CML/2022/52 dated November 04, 2022 specifying consequences of non- compliance with the requirements of Reg 3(5) and 3(6) specifies consequences of non-compliance with the requirements of Reg 3(5) and 3(6) of SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015. Further to above mentioned Circulars, the companies are advised to take a note of the following: 1) The listed entities to whom the provisions of Regulation 24A of SEBI(LODR) Regulations, 2015 are applicable, the Secretarial Auditor of those entities shall also specifically confirm compliance with the requirement of SDD by the listed entities in its Annual Secretarial Audit Report. Listed companies are advised to bring to the knowledge of their Secretarial Auditor the above requirement. 2) Exchange circular no. NSE/CML/2022/52 dated November 04, 2022 specifies consequences of non-compliance with Reg 3(5) and 3(6) of SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 states as under: “Under the “Get Quote” page of the Exchange Website of the Listed Entity, wherever listed, would display that the company is non-compliant with SDD, from the next trading day till the Exchanges have satisfactorily verified that the company has completely complied.” It is clarified that in addition to above, the name of the compliance officer will also be displayed on the “Get Quote” page of the Exchange website where the above information is disseminated. The circular shall be effective immediately. All Listed companies are requested to take note and comply accordingly. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Yogesh Deshmukh Senior Manager
rows.summary:
This circular requires all listed entities to note and comply with the existing Structured Digital Database (SDD) obligations under Regulations 3(5) and 3(6) of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, and it updates how compliance will be evidenced and displayed by the Exchange. For listed entities that are subject to Regulation 24A of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, the Secretarial Auditor must now specifically confirm SDD compliance in the Annual Secretarial Audit Report; companies should proactively inform their Secretarial Auditor of this requirement so it is explicitly covered in the audit.  

The circular also reiterates the Exchange’s non-compliance consequences under its earlier Circular No. NSE/CML/2022/52 dated November 4, 2022: if a listed company is found non-compliant with Reg. 3(5) and 3(6), the Exchange will display on the company’s “Get Quote” page that the company is non-compliant with SDD, starting from the next trading day and continuing until the Exchange has satisfactorily verified full compliance. In addition to the company-level non-compliance notice, the circular clarifies that the name of the compliance officer will also be displayed on the same “Get Quote” page where this information is published.  

The circular references earlier NSE communications that set timelines for submitting the SDD Compliance Certificate for the quarters ended September 30, 2022 and December 31, 2022, and it is intended as a further compliance advisory on top of those prior directions. No new monetary threshold is introduced, but the operational impact is significant because failure to maintain or demonstrate SDD compliance may now result in public disclosure on the Exchange website linked both to the company and the compliance officer. The circular is effective immediately and applies to all listed companies.

rows.title: Facility of conducting meetings of unit holders of REITs through Video Conferencing or Other Audio-Visual means
rows.desc: Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No: NSE/CML/2023/08 Date: 13 January, 2023 The Company Secretary All Listed Companies Subject: Facility of conducting meetings of unit holders of REITs through Video Conferencing or Other Audio-Visual means Dear Sir/ Madam, This is with reference to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div2/P/CIR/2023/13 dated January 12, 2023 issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) titled “Facility of conducting meetings of unit holders of REITs through Video Conferencing or Other Audio- Visual means” A copy of SEBI Circular dated January 12, 2023 is enclosed for your reference and for necessary action at your end. The copy of the circular is also available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com). This is for your information please. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. Sandeep Dhamal Manager
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated 13 January 2023 is a forwarding communication to all listed companies from the National Stock Exchange of India, alerting them to a SEBI circular issued one day earlier, on 12 January 2023, titled “Facility of conducting meetings of unit holders of REITs through Video Conferencing or Other Audio-Visual means.” The NSE letter itself does not impose new substantive obligations; it informs recipients that SEBI has issued the referenced circular and that a copy is enclosed and available on the NSE website for necessary action.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the underlying SEBI circular concerns Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and the manner in which meetings of REIT unit holders may be conducted, specifically permitting meetings through video conferencing or other audio-visual means. No implementation deadline, threshold, rate, or procedural detail is stated in the NSE cover note itself, and the document does not specify which listed entities beyond REIT-related stakeholders are directly affected. A compliance officer would need to review the attached SEBI circular dated 12 January 2023 to determine the precise meeting-process requirements, any conditions for using electronic modes, and any timeline for adoption or compliance.
