rows.title: Circular for seeking of comments / feedback on the XBRL being introduced for submission of Announcements pertaining to Corporate Debt Restructuring
rows.desc: Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/06 Date: January 11, 2023 The Company Secretary All Listed Companies Subject: Seeking of comments / feedback on the XBRL being introduced for submission of Announcements pertaining to Corporate Debt Restructuring 1. OBJECTIVE: The objective of this document is to seek comments / feedback on the proposal to migrate from Portable Document Format (PDF) to eXtensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) format for submitting corporate announcements pertaining to Corporate Debt Restructuring as required under the provisions of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (LODR) read alongwith SEBI Circular dated September 09, 2015, as amended from time to time and such applicable laws. 2. BACKGROUND: Listed entities are required to submit periodical compliance filings to Stock Exchange(s) within prescribed timelines as laid down in SEBI Listing Regulations and accordingly it was mandated to report XBRL based filings for financials from year 2015 onwards. Over the period, Stock Exchanges in phased manner has been aiming to convert filings made under SEBI Regulations from PDF to XBRL. Listed entities file various disclosures under Regulation 30 of LODR with such details as are sought under the applicable Regulations/Circulars. With an objective to standardise securities market data it was deliberated that XBRL would be implemented for all corporate filings. Accordingly, Stock Exchanges have implemented XBRL based compliance filing mechanism featuring identical and homogenous compliance data structures which will not only ease the compliance burden on listed entities but also will enable analysis on the data submitted by the listed entities. Hence, in this regard filing of announcements pertaining to Corporate Debt Restructuring would require listed entities to file the same in XBRL exclusively, formats of which are made available in para 4 hereinbelow. 3. ISSUES AND DELIBERATIONS: Please note that the details required are typically descriptive in nature and based on the LODR Regulations and the applicable SEBI Circulars. Accordingly, listed entities can provide their comments/feedback/suggestions/observations pertaining to any additions/modifications in the fields of the attached format. 4. COMMENTS FROM LISTED ENTITIES Considering the implications of the XBRL filing by listed entities, comments in respect of the subject are solicited. Comments may be sent by email to DL-Announcement@nse.co.in in the following format: Name of entity / person: Contact Number & Email Address: Sr. No Event: Corporate Debt Restructuring Subject/Heading/ Field Comments/ Suggestions Detailed Rationale While sending email, kindly mention the subject as “Comments / Feedback on the XBRL being introduced for Corporate Debt Restructuring” The comments may be sent by email to DL-Announcement@nse.co.in latest by January 13, 2023. Enclosed is the draft format for the XBRL being introduced. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Dhaval Shah Manager – Listing Encl: Draft Format for XBRL being introduced for Corporate Debt Restructuring. CORPORATE DEBT RESTRUCTURING PARTICULARS SUB-PARTICULARS General Information NSE Symbol Name of the Company BSE Scrip Code MSE Symbol ISIN Stage of Disclosure 1. Initial 2. Update Type of Disclosure 1. New 2. Revision Date of initial announcement Date of latest announcement Remarks (website dissemination) Remarks for Exchange (not for Website Dissemination) Date of Report Corporate Debt Restructuring Details- Initial Whether the Corporate debt restructuring is Voluntary or Referred by Lenders/Creditors 1. Voluntary 2. Referred by Lenders/Creditors Date of Board Meeting in which CDR was approved Reasons for opting CDR Details of Lenders/Creditors referring Corporate Debt Restructuring of the Company Details of the Loan to be subjected to Corporate Debt Restructuring Brief details of the Corporate Debt Restructuring proposal (if any) Corporate Debt Restructuring Details- Update Stage of the implementation of the CDR scheme 1. Execution 2. Others Execution of the CDR Scheme Date of execution of the agreement Parties to the agreement Principal terms of the agreement Brief summary of the agreement executed under Corporate Debt Restructuring Scheme Others Details of final CDR package as approved by RBI and the lenders Details of Lenders involved in Corporate Debt Restructuring Brief summary of the Corporate Debt Restructuring Scheme Details of the securities involved in Corporate Debt Restructuring Details of the interest payment and/or repayment schedule Details of the negative and other restrictive covenants Any other disclosure w.r.t. compliance of any SEBI Act, Regulation, Circular or provision Any other information Remarks (for Website dissemination) Remarks for Exchange (not for website dissemination)
rows.summary:
This circular, issued by NSE on January 11, 2023, does not itself impose a finalized rule change; it seeks comments and feedback from listed entities on a proposal to migrate corporate announcements relating to Corporate Debt Restructuring (CDR) from PDF submissions to an XBRL-only filing format under SEBI LODR Regulation 30 and the relevant SEBI circulars. The practical change being proposed is that CDR announcements would no longer be filed as free-form PDF disclosures; instead, listed companies would be required to submit the information in a standardized XBRL template so the stock exchange can capture structured, comparable data across issuers.

The circular makes clear that the affected parties are listed entities that make CDR-related announcements, whether the CDR is voluntary or referred by lenders/creditors. It explains that this proposal is part of a broader exchange effort to convert disclosure filings from PDF to XBRL, following the earlier implementation of XBRL-based reporting for financial filings from 2015 onward, with the stated goals of standardizing market data, easing compliance burden, and improving data analysis. No penalty or implementation date for mandatory filing is stated in this document; instead, the current deadline is for feedback on the draft format.

Comments, suggestions, and observations were requested by email to DL-Announcement@nse.co.in no later than January 13, 2023, and the email subject line had to read “Comments / Feedback on the XBRL being introduced for Corporate Debt Restructuring.” The circular also specifies the information the draft XBRL template would require: general identifiers such as NSE symbol, company name, BSE scrip code, MSE symbol, ISIN, disclosure stage (initial or update), disclosure type (new or revision), dates of the initial and latest announcements, and separate remarks fields for website dissemination versus exchange-only use, along with the date of report. For an initial CDR disclosure, the template asks whether the restructuring is voluntary or lender/creditor-referred, the date of the board meeting approving CDR, reasons for opting for CDR, details of the referring lenders/creditors, details of the loan subject to restructuring, and a brief description of the proposal. For update disclosures, it requires the implementation stage of the scheme, execution date of the agreement, parties, principal terms, a summary of the executed agreement, and, where applicable, final RBI/lender-approved package details, lender names, securities involved, interest and repayment schedules, negative/restrictive covenants, any other SEBI compliance disclosures, and any additional information, again with separate website and exchange-only remarks fields.

rows.title: Comprehensive Framework on Offer for Sale (OFS) of Shares through Stock Exchange Mechanism
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: LISTING Download Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/05 Date: January 11, 2023 To All Members, Subject: Comprehensive Framework on Offer for Sale (OFS) of Shares through Stock Exchange Mechanism Dear Sir/ Madam, This is with reference to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/MRD/MRD-PoD-3/P/CIR/2023/10 dated January 10, 2023 issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) titled “Comprehensive Framework on Offer for Sale (OFS) of Shares through Stock Exchange Mechanism.” A copy of SEBI Circular dated January 10, 2023 is enclosed for your reference and for necessary action at your end. The copy of the circular is also available on the NSE website (www.nseindia.com). This is for your information please. Yours faithfully For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Sandeep Dhamal Manager
rows.summary:
This NSE communication is a forwarding notice, not a new rule in itself. It informs all members that SEBI issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/MRD/MRD-PoD-3/P/CIR/2023/10 on January 10, 2023, titled “Comprehensive Framework on Offer for Sale (OFS) of Shares through Stock Exchange Mechanism,” and that the SEBI circular is enclosed and available on the NSE website for reference and necessary action.

For a compliance team, the key point is that any entity using, facilitating, or participating in the stock-exchange mechanism for an OFS must review and implement the SEBI framework referenced in the January 10, 2023 circular. However, this NSE note itself does not describe the substantive OFS requirements, procedural changes, thresholds, deadlines, or affected issuer categories; it only confirms that SEBI has issued the framework and that members should take action as required by that underlying SEBI circular. No separate effective date beyond the SEBI circular date of January 10, 2023 is stated in this notice, and no additional numerical limits or operational instructions appear in the text provided.

rows.summary:
NSE Circular No. **NSE/CML/2023/04** dated **January 10, 2023** is a **consultation circular**, not yet a final implementation notice, seeking comments from listed companies on a proposal to move from **PDF to XBRL** for submitting **corporate announcements relating to notices of shareholders’ meetings** under the **SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015** and the SEBI circular dated **September 9, 2015**, as amended. The exchange says the broader policy direction is to standardize market data and reduce compliance burden by using a uniform XBRL filing structure, building on the XBRL-based filing framework already used for financial reporting since 2015 and being expanded in phases to other LODR disclosures.

For the specific item covered in this consultation, the proposed change is that announcements for **all notices of shareholders’ meetings** would be filed **exclusively in XBRL**, initially in **Phase I**, where only the **agenda heading details** are captured; **Phase II**, which would capture **all details forming part of the notice**, is stated to come later in a separate circular. The draft XBRL template attached to the circular shows that the filing would require basic company and event identification fields such as **NSE symbol, company name, BSE scrip code, MSE symbol, ISIN, event type** (AGM, EGM, postal ballot, NCLT/court-convened meeting, or others), **mode of meeting** (physical or VC/OAVM), **meeting date/time/place**, **postal ballot voting end date**, and the **number of agenda/business items**. It also requires disclosure of the **resolution/agenda type** (ordinary resolution, special resolution, others) and a **resolution header/searchable content**, with dropdown-based standardized resolution headings.

The draft annexure indicates that the “ordinary resolution” dropdown/category includes items such as **adoption of financial statements, appointment/re-appointment of directors and auditors, bonus issue, dividend declaration/confirmation, change in authorized capital, donation to charitable trusts, office of profit, promoter re-classification, remuneration/ratification of statutory auditors**, and related governance items; the list continues beyond the excerpt provided. The circular further distinguishes between **“remarks (website dissemination)”** and **“remarks for exchange (not for website dissemination)”**, so companies would need to prepare content with the correct disclosure channel in mind. NSE requests that listed entities send **comments, feedback, suggestions, or observations** on the Phase I draft format by email to **DL-Announcement@nse.co.in**, using the subject line **“Comments / Feedback on the XBRL being introduced for notice of shareholders meeting”**, and the deadline for submission is **January 12, 2023**. The circular is addressed to **all listed companies**, but it is explicitly a request for input on the proposed phased XBRL reporting structure rather than an immediate operative compliance mandate.

rows.title: Filing of SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 disclosure to Exchange
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: LISTING Download Ref No: NSE/CML/2023/03 Date: January 06, 2023 To All Members, Subject: Filing of SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 disclosures to Exchange This is in continuation to Exchange Circular no NSE/CML/2022/03 dated January 06, 2022, and Circular Ref. No: NSE/CML/2022/09 dated February 17, 2022, informing about the launch of New Digital Portal which was made live for filings with the Exchange. With reference to above filing of disclosure under SEBI (SAST) Regulations, 2011 will now required to be filed on Takeover Email ID (takeover@nse.co.in) with effect from January 07, 2023. Contact details of the Exchange Officers are available on the NEAPS portal and the companies can get in touch with the respective officers for issues and queries pertaining to filings of SEBI (SAST) Regulations, 2011. Yours faithfully For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Yogesh Deshmukh Senior Manager
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India is changing the filing process for disclosures made under the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011. Effective **January 07, 2023**, such SAST disclosures must be submitted to the Exchange via the dedicated **Takeover email ID: takeover@nse.co.in**, rather than through the earlier filing route referenced in the Exchange’s prior circulars on the new digital portal.

This circular is a continuation of NSE Circular No. **NSE/CML/2022/03 dated January 06, 2022** and Circular Ref. No. **NSE/CML/2022/09 dated February 17, 2022**, which had informed members about the launch of the Exchange’s new digital portal for filings. The document does not change the underlying SEBI SAST disclosure obligations themselves; it changes the **submission channel** for those disclosures to the Exchange. Companies required to make SAST filings should direct all such filings to the takeover email address starting on the effective date.

For compliance purposes, the Exchange also notes that relevant contact details for Exchange officers are available on the **NEAPS portal**, and companies may contact the designated officers for issues and queries related to SEBI (SAST) filings.

rows.summary:
This NSE circular (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2023/01 dated January 5, 2023) is a consultation notice to all listed companies seeking comments on a proposal to replace PDF-based corporate announcement filings with XBRL-only submissions for a defined set of Regulation 30/LODR events. The proposed XBRL migration would apply to announcements relating to issuance or forfeiture of securities, split or consolidation of shares, alterations in capital, actions that change the terms or structure of existing securities, restrictions on transferability of securities, reissue of forfeited securities, alterations of calls, redemption of securities, and similar events under the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 and the relevant SEBI circulars.

For compliance teams, the key change is that these announcements would no longer be filed in PDF format but would need to be submitted exclusively in XBRL, using the standardised data fields being drafted by the exchanges. The circular explains that the purpose is to standardise securities-market data, reduce compliance burden over time, and enable more uniform analysis of listed entities’ disclosures; it also notes that listed entities already file XBRL for financial filings and that exchanges have been moving other SEBI-regulated filings from PDF to XBRL in phases. The draft XBRL template attached to the circular shows that the filing will require structured fields such as NSE symbol, company name, BSE scrip code, MSE symbol, ISIN, event type, and detailed event-specific information.

The consultation specifically asks listed entities to comment on the proposed fields, including any additions, modifications, or other observations, because the data requirements are described as largely based on existing LODR provisions and SEBI circular requirements. Comments must be emailed to DL-Announcement@nse.co.in in the prescribed format identifying the entity/person, contact number and email, the event category, the relevant subject/heading/field, the suggested change, and the detailed rationale. When sending comments, the subject line must read: “Comments / Feedback on the XBRL being introduced for issuance or forfeiture of securities, alteration, any restriction on transferability of securities”.

The deadline for submitting feedback was January 8, 2023. The circular is signed by National Stock Exchange of India Limited and encloses the draft XBRL format for the proposed announcement types; the visible portion of the draft shows, for example, that fund-raising/issuance filings will need event classification such as new issuance versus cancellation/termination, the reasons for cancellation, board meeting date and times, and whether prior intimation of the board meeting was given to the stock exchange.

rows.title: Revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on application filed under Regulation 37 and 59A of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 w.r.t. Scheme of Arrangements.
rows.desc: Circular Department: LISTING Download Ref No: NSE/CML/2022/61 Date: December 20, 2022 The Company Secretary All Listed Companies Subject: - Revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on application filed under Regulation 37 and 59A of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 w.r.t. Scheme of Arrangements. This has reference to the draft scheme of arrangement filed with stock exchanges under Regulation 37 and 59A of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 read along with SEBI Master Circulars dated November 23, 2021 and amendment thereof and NSE circular NSE/CML/2021/43 dated November 02, 2021 and SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS- RACPOD1/P/CIR/2022/156 dated November 17, 2022. In this regard, kindly find below the revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) to be followed by listed entities: 1. The Scheme of Arrangement seeking Stock Exchange’s NOC under Regulation 37 and Regulation 59A of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘SEBI LODR’) shall be submitted to the Exchange along with all the documents as per the Exchange Checklist within 15 working days of board meeting approving the draft scheme of arrangement. In case the application is not submitted within 15 working days, the company shall take fresh approval from its board considering fresh financials, valuation report, etc. 2. At the time of submission of the application to the Exchange(s) under Regulation 37 and regulation 59A of SEBI LODR, the Audited Financials of last 3 years (financials not being older than 6 months) of unlisted company(ies) involved in the Scheme of Arrangement has to be submitted as required under para I (A) (2) (f) of SEBI Circular dated March 10, 2017 and amendment thereof read with SEBI Master Circular dated November 23, 2021 and para 1 (A) (2) (e) of SEBI circular SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-RACPOD1/P/CIR/2022/156 dated November 17, 2022. The aforesaid audited financials shall be considered for preparation of Valuation Report by the valuer under Income Approach. At the time of providing its observation letter to the listed entity, the exchange shall seek an undertaking from the listed entity stating that it shall ensure that the financials of the unlisted company(ies) shall not be more than 6 months old at the time of submission of the scheme papers to NCLT. 3. The audited financials considered for valuations, other than Income Approach, should not be older than 3 months. The board shall consider the scheme of arrangement within 7 working days of the issuance of valuation report. 4. At the time of submission of application with the stock exchange(s) under: i. Regulation 37: documents referred in para (I) (A) (2) of SEBI Master Circular dated November 23, 2021 (as amended) and included in the checklist of respective stock exchange(s), should be complete in all aspects. ii. Regulation 59A: documents refereed in para (I) (A) (2) of SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-RACPOD1/P/CIR/2022/156 dated November 17, 2022 and included in the checklist of the respective stock exchange(s), should be complete in all aspects. Note: For Listed Entity having their specified securities as well as NCDs/NCRPS listed, a single filing of the draft scheme of arrangement in terms of Regulations 37 and Regulation 59A of SEBI LODR Regulation 2015 shall be submitted under Regulation 37 wherein additional documents, as required for Debt Listed company shall also be attached. 5. Exchange Queries: - If the documents (referred in point no.4) are incomplete or any clarification needed or any material inadequacies/non-compliance with the SEBI Circulars are observed in the documents by the Exchange, the scheme shall be returned to the Company for necessary rectifications. A period of 7 working days for applications filed under Regulation 37 and Regulation 59A will be allowed to the company for rectification. On expiry of aforesaid timelines if the company is unable to make submissions, then any fees paid by the Company for processing of the application shall be forfeited by the Exchange/Regulator and the scheme documents shall be returned to the company. 6. For only Debt Listed Entities: The Listed Entity shall submit their revert to queries (if any) raised by the Stock Exchange as early as possible, to enable adherence to requirement of “maximum number of days for providing the ‘No-Objection’ Letter to SEBI shall not exceed thirty days from the date of receipt of the draft scheme of arrangement”. 7. If appropriate responses are not received by the Exchanges within the timelines, the Company may be asked to re-file the scheme with requisite rectifications as a fresh application and any fees paid by the Company for processing of the application shall be forfeited by the Exchange/Regulator. 8. Any refiling because of the previous unsatisfactory filing shall be made along with fresh set of valuation report, fairness opinion, recommendation of the audit committee, etc. The company
rows.summary:
This circular, effective from **December 20, 2022**, issues a **revised standard operating procedure (SOP)** for listed entities seeking a stock exchange **No-Objection Certificate (NOC)** for a **scheme of arrangement** filed under **Regulation 37** and, where applicable, **Regulation 59A** of the **SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**. A draft scheme must be filed with the exchange **within 15 working days of the board meeting** approving the draft scheme; if that deadline is missed, the company must obtain **fresh board approval** based on **updated financials, valuation report, etc.** The filing must be complete and include all documents required under the relevant exchange checklist and the cited SEBI circulars.

For schemes involving **unlisted company(ies)**, the company must submit the **audited financials of the last 3 years**, and those financials must **not be older than 6 months** at the time of submission; these financials are specifically to be used by the valuer for the **Income Approach**. When the exchange issues its observation letter, it will require an **undertaking** from the listed entity confirming that the unlisted company financials will still be **no more than 6 months old when the scheme papers are filed with NCLT**. For valuation methods **other than the Income Approach**, the audited financials used for valuation must be **no older than 3 months**. In addition, the board must consider the scheme **within 7 working days of the valuation report being issued**.

The SOP also tightens the completeness and submission requirements at the exchange level: under **Regulation 37**, the documents listed in **para (I)(A)(2) of the SEBI Master Circular dated November 23, 2021 (as amended)** must be fully complete; under **Regulation 59A**, the documents in **para (I)(A)(2) of SEBI Circular dated November 17, 2022** must be fully complete. If a listed entity has both **specified securities** and **NCDs/NCRPS** listed, it must make a **single filing under Regulation 37**, and also attach the **additional documents required for debt-listed companies**.

If the exchange finds missing documents, requests clarifications, or identifies material inadequacies or non-compliance, it will return the scheme for rectification and allow the company **7 working days** to cure the defects. If the company does not respond within that period, any **fees paid for processing will be forfeited** and the scheme documents will be returned. For **debt-listed entities**, the company must respond to exchange queries **as early as possible** so that the exchange can meet the requirement that the **NOC to SEBI must be issued within 30 days from receipt of the draft scheme**. If responses are still not provided in time, the company may have to **re-file the scheme as a fresh application**, and the **processing fees will again be forfeited**; any such refiling must include a **fresh valuation report, fairness opinion, audit committee recommendation, and related documents**.

rows.title: Clarifications with respect to SEBI Circular no. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHSRACPOD1/P/CIR/2022/156 dated November 17, 2022 (“SEBI Circular”), on Scheme(s) of Arrangement by entities who have listed their Non-convertible Debt securities (NCDs)/ Non-convertible Redeemable Preference shares (NCRPS)’
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: Download Ref No: NSE/CML/2022/59 Date: December 19, 2022 To, The Listed Entities Subject: Clarifications with respect to SEBI Circular no. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS- RACPOD1/P/CIR/2022/156 dated November 17, 2022 (“SEBI Circular”), on Scheme(s) of Arrangement by entities who have listed their Non-convertible Debt securities (NCDs)/ Non- convertible Redeemable Preference shares (NCRPS)’ SEBI, vide Circular no. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-RACPOD1/P/CIR/2022/156 dated November 17, 2022, has laid down procedure on Scheme(s) of Arrangement by entities who have listed their Non- convertible Debt securities (NCDs)/ Non-convertible Redeemable Preference shares (NCRPS) to implement amendment w.r.t. regulation 59A/94A in Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. For implementation of the aforesaid SEBI circular, following clarifications are hereby provided to the issuers: 1. Applicability: The said regulation/circular shall be applicable to the Listed Entity whose Board Meeting approving the Scheme of Arrangement was/is held after November 14, 2022, i.e. date of amendment in Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. 2. Report of Complaints/ Comments received by the listed entity on the draft scheme of arrangement: For Listed Entity having their specified securities as well as NCDs/NCRPS listed must submit the report on Complaints to the Stock Exchanges within 7 days of expiry of 21 days from the date of hosting the draft scheme along with documents on the website of Stock Exchanges and the listed entity. For Listed Entity having only their NCDs /NCRPS listed must submit the report on Complaints to the Stock Exchanges within 7 days of expiry of 10 days from the date of hosting the draft scheme along with documents on the websites of Stock Exchanges and the listed entity. Continuation Sheet 3. Timelines: The Listed Entity shall submit their revert to queries (if any) raised by the Stock Exchange within 7 working days of query being raised, to enable adherence to requirement of “maximum number of days for providing the ‘No-Objection’ Letter to SEBI shall not exceed thirty days from the date of receipt of the draft scheme of arrangement”. It may be noted that submission of incomplete reply will be considered as non-submission. These timelines are applicable to issuers with only NCDs /NCRPS listed. For specified securities timelines as mentioned in our joint SOP shall prevail. 4. Number of applications: For Listed Entity having their specified securities as well as NCDs/NCRPS listed, a single filing of the draft scheme of arrangement in terms of Regulations 37 and Regulation 59A of SEBI LODR Regulation 2015 shall be submitted under Regulation 37 wherein additional documents, as required for NCDs/NCRPS listed company shall also be attached. 5. Exemption from usage of Electronic Bidding Platform: Wherein under the scheme of arrangement, the issuers propose to raise further NCDs without using EBP platform, exemption from the requirements of usage of Electronic Bidding Platform (“EBP”) should be obtained by the issuer from SEBI. 6. Approval from the debenture holders: Under SEBI circular dated November 17, 2022, Point No. 12, wherein approval of the debenture holders is required, the value of the same shall be governed as stated under Companies Act, 2013 i.e. Section 230. 7. Exit offer to the dissenting holders of NCDs/ NCRPSAs Exit offer to the dissenting holders of NCDs/ NCRPSAs specified Para 2(d)(iii) of Annexure-I of SEBI Circular, while recommending the draft scheme, the Board of Directors shall also comment on Exit offer to be dissenting holders of NCDs/ NCRPS, if any. Further, if there is provisions related to exit offer, same shall also be part of the scheme. This is for your information please. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Dipti Chinchkhede Manager
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated December 19, 2022 provides implementation clarifications for SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-RACPOD1/P/CIR/2022/156 dated November 17, 2022, which introduced the procedure for schemes of arrangement involving entities that have listed non-convertible debt securities (NCDs) and/or non-convertible redeemable preference shares (NCRPS) under the amended LODR provisions (Regulations 59A/94A). The clarified requirements apply only to listed entities whose Board meeting approving the scheme of arrangement was held after November 14, 2022, which is the effective date of the relevant amendment to the SEBI LODR Regulations.

For the draft scheme comment process, entities with both specified securities and NCDs/NCRPS listed must submit the report on complaints/comments to the stock exchanges within 7 days after the expiry of the 21-day public posting period for the draft scheme on the websites of the stock exchanges and the listed entity. Entities that have only NCDs/NCRPS listed must submit the complaints/comments report within 7 days after the expiry of a 10-day posting period. This means the public consultation period differs depending on whether the company also has listed specified securities, and the submission deadline runs from the end of that applicable posting period.

On timelines for stock exchange queries, issuers with only NCDs/NCRPS listed must respond to any stock exchange queries within 7 working days of the query being raised; incomplete replies will be treated as non-submission. This is tied to the requirement that the “No-Objection” letter to SEBI must be issued within a maximum of 30 days from receipt of the draft scheme of arrangement. The circular also clarifies that these response timelines apply only to issuers with only NCDs/NCRPS listed, while for entities with specified securities the timelines set out in the joint SOP continue to govern.

For filing mechanics, listed entities with both specified securities and NCDs/NCRPS are required to make a single filing of the draft scheme under Regulation 37, and that filing must also include the additional documents required for an NCD/NCRPS-listed company under Regulation 59A. If, under a scheme of arrangement, the issuer proposes to raise further NCDs without using the Electronic Bidding Platform (EBP), it must separately obtain an exemption from SEBI from the EBP requirement.

The circular also clarifies that where debenture-holder approval is required under Point 12 of the SEBI circular, the valuation/threshold for that approval is to be determined in accordance with Section 230 of the Companies Act, 2013. Finally, if the scheme provides for an exit offer to dissenting holders of NCDs/NCRPS, the Board of Directors must specifically comment on that exit offer when recommending the draft scheme, and any such exit-offer provision must be expressly included in the scheme itself.

rows.title: Circular pertaining to submission of the Aadhar details in the Announcement/Offer Documents submitted to the Exchange.
rows.desc: 1 CIRCULAR Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2022/60 Date: December 19, 2022 The Company Secretary, All Listed Entities, Entities/Issuers who propose to list their securities with the Exchange. Subject: Submission of the Aadhar numbers in the Announcements / Offer Documents submitted to the Exchange Dear Sir/ Madam, As per Section 29(4) of the Aadhaar Act, 2016 (as amended in 2019) (hereinafter referred to as the “Aadhaar Act”), no Aadhaar number or demographic information or photograph collected or created under the Aadhaar Act is to be disclosed publicly, except for the purpose specified in the said Aadhaar Act. Further, the Acts and Rules governing the Organization/Institution that mandate the requirement of publishing Aadhaar information, shall be published in masked form. The Exchange has observed that: 1. Listed entities are disclosing certain Aadhar numbers/ Aadhar cards in their announcements specifically in the cases of newspaper publications where the clipping has other news lines related to Aadhar number. In such cases, entities should only disclose the newspaper clipping related to itself and should abstain from submitting the entire page of the newspaper containing other details. 2. Entities/Issuers proposing to list any of their securities with the Exchange are disclosing Aadhar numbers/ Aadhar related information in the draft offer documents/offer documents submitted to the Exchange. In this regard, kindly also note that Aadhar number/ Aadhar information of the promoters/others as required under the applicable SEBI regulations viz. SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, SEBI (Issue and Listing of Non-Convertible Securities) Regulations, 2021 etc. are to be provided to the Exchange separately and should not be disclosed in the draft offer document/offer document/any other public document. In view of the above, all listed entities/issuers proposing to list their securities with the Exchange, are hereby advised to strictly adhere to the aforesaid provisions of Aadhar Act and not disclose Aadhar number/Aadhar related information in any disclosure/ announcements/ any other public document made/submitted to the Exchange. You are requested to kindly take note of the contents of this circular and ensure compliance of the same with immediate effect. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Avishkar Naik Head – Listing Compliance
rows.summary:
This NSE Listing Circular (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2022/60, dated December 19, 2022) requires all listed entities and all issuers proposing to list securities with the Exchange to stop disclosing Aadhaar numbers or any Aadhaar-related information in announcements, offer documents, or any other public document submitted to the Exchange, with immediate effect. The circular is based on Section 29(4) of the Aadhaar Act, 2016 (as amended in 2019), which prohibits public disclosure of Aadhaar numbers, demographic information, or photographs collected under the Act except as specifically permitted, and further requires any Aadhaar information that must be published under other applicable laws to be published only in masked form.

For listed entities, the Exchange specifically observed that some are submitting newspaper clippings that contain Aadhaar numbers or Aadhaar cards along with unrelated news on the same page; the circular directs entities to submit only the clipping relevant to their own announcement and not the full newspaper page. For entities/issuers preparing draft offer documents or offer documents, the circular says Aadhaar numbers or Aadhaar-related information of promoters or others that are required under applicable SEBI regulations (including the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018 and the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Non-Convertible Securities) Regulations, 2021) must be provided to the Exchange separately, and must not appear in the draft offer document, offer document, or any other public document.

In practical compliance terms, the document imposes an immediate obligation to review all submissions to the Exchange and ensure that any Aadhaar references are removed from public-facing materials or masked where disclosure is legally required, while any required Aadhaar details are routed separately to the Exchange through non-public channels. The circular is directed to Company Secretaries of all listed entities and prospective issuers, and it is a mandatory compliance instruction rather than a discretionary best practice.

rows.title: Circular for filing of Equity announcements and Financial Results to be made available on the NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System) platform
rows.desc: CIRCULAR Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2022/58 Date: December 15, 2022 To, All Listed Companies Dear Sir/Madam, Subject: Filing of Equity announcements and Financial Results to be made available on the NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System) platform. This is in continuation to Exchange Circular no NSE/CML/2022/03 dated January 06, 2022, Circular Ref. No: NSE/CML/2022/09 dated February 17, 2022, and Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2022/34 dated July 08, 2022, informing about the launch of New Digital Portal which was made live for filings with the Exchange. With reference to the above and to bring all the filings under one single portal, it has been decided by the Exchange that filings for the Equity Announcements and Financial Results will be made available only on NEAPS portal with effect from December 17, 2022. Henceforth, the Companies will have to file their disclosures for the Equity Announcements subjects and Financial Results in the same manner as it was available on the NEAPS platform in the month of February 2022. Further, this is to clarify that: - For outcome of board meeting with only financial results as agenda item as Quarterly/Half yearly/Annual Financial results (PDF file) will have to be filed only under Quick Results module on NEAPS. - For outcome of board meeting with multiple agenda item along with financial results will have to filed under both Announcement and Quick result module on NEAPS. - Furthermore, the XBRL submission for the Financial Results will have to be filed under Full Results module on NEAPS. Contact details of the Exchange Officers for the respective subjects are available on the NEAPS portal and the companies can get in touch with the respective officers for the issues and queries pertaining to filings on the NEAPS platform. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Avishkar Naik Head – Listing Compliance
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India Limited issued this circular to move all **Equity Announcements** and **Financial Results** filings onto the **NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System) portal only**, consolidating these submissions under a single platform. This change applies to **all listed companies** and becomes effective **December 17, 2022**. The circular states that filings must now be made in the same manner as was available on NEAPS in **February 2022**, and it is a continuation of earlier circulars dated **January 6, 2022 (NSE/CML/2022/03)**, **February 17, 2022 (NSE/CML/2022/09)**, and **July 8, 2022 (NSE/CML/2022/34)** regarding the new digital portal.

The circular then specifies the filing procedure depending on the board meeting agenda. If the board meeting outcome contains **only financial results** as the agenda item, the company must file the **quarterly, half-yearly, or annual financial results in PDF format only under the “Quick Results” module** on NEAPS. If the board meeting outcome includes **multiple agenda items along with financial results**, the company must file the disclosure **both under the “Announcement” module and the “Quick Result” module** on NEAPS. In addition, the **XBRL version of the financial results** must be filed under the **“Full Results” module** on NEAPS.

For operational support, the Exchange notes that the **contact details of the relevant Exchange officers are available on the NEAPS portal**, and companies are expected to use those contacts for issues and queries related to filings on the platform. The compliance implication is that companies should transition any remaining Equity Announcement and Financial Results workflows to NEAPS by the effective date and ensure internal filing procedures distinguish between single-agenda financial results filings, multi-agenda board outcomes, and XBRL submissions so that each is submitted in the correct NEAPS module.

rows.title: FAQ’s - Disclosure of holding of specified securities and Holding of specified securities in dematerialized form
rows.desc: Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref. No.: NSE/CML/2022/57 Date: December 14, 2022 The Company Secretary All Listed Companies Subject: FAQ’s - Disclosure of holding of specified securities and Holding of specified securities in dematerialized form Dear Sir/ Madam, This is in reference to the general guidelines in relation with filing Shareholding Pattern report as per Regulation 31 of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirement) Regulations, 2015. Please find annexed updated frequently asked questions (FAQs) basis past observations on Shareholding Pattern Report. Companies are requested to comply with the requirement of listing regulations and other applicable regulations as amended from time to time. The FAQ’s can be referred only for the guidance purpose. This is for your information please. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Sailee Pawaskar Manager Annexure General FAQs: 1. How to distinguish a deceased person in shareholding pattern in case Promoter/Promoter Group is Individual? In an event of demise of an individual belonging to Promoter or Promoter Group where the shares held by such individual are not transmitted to the legal heir as on the end of the quarter, the company should disclose detailed notes for the same in the shareholding pattern. Upon transmission of the shares to the legal heir(s), the company can exclude names of the Late Promoter/Promoter Group(s) individual from the forthcoming shareholding pattern, while including the name of legal heir the Company should mention detailed note about the transmission of shares. Further, till the time shares are not transmitted to the legal heir, the name(s) of deceased person should be continued to be included in Promoter/Promoter Group(s) while filing shareholding pattern with the Stock Exchange. 2. How to disclose name of Promoter/Promoter Group Company in shareholding pattern which got wound up or dissolved post-merger / amalgamation? In an event, the list of Promoter / Promoter Group includes Company which get wound up or dissolved, the Company should mention detailed note(s) while filing shareholding pattern from forthcoming quarter. 3. If a shareholder has already been disclosed in Table II (Statement showing shareholding pattern of the Promoter and Promoter Group) and also falls into one of the categories in Table III (Statement showing shareholding pattern of the public shareholder), should they be disclosed again in Table III? No. Any shareholder whose shareholding has already been disclosed in Table II should not be disclosed again in Table III. In other words, any shareholder falling under the definition of "promoter" or "promoter group" should not be disclosed in Table III. 4. If a shareholder is falling under more than one category in Table III, then the same shall be classified under which category? Categorization and disclosure of each shareholding category should be carried out in the order prescribed in the format of the shareholding pattern. If a shareholder is falling under more than one category, then the same shall be classified in the category falling first in the order prescribed in the format. Shareholding under any of the categories shall be unique and will not be duplicated under multiple categories. 5. How do we report sub-categorization of shares under column no. (XV) in Table III in case any shareholder category comprises of multiple sub-categories? In case any shareholder category comprises of multiple sub-categories, shareholding (no. of shares) under each sub-category needs to be separately included under the respective sub-categories under column no. (XV). 6. Can the name of the promoter be removed from the Shareholding Pattern during the Quarter in case the Shares are transferred/sold? The name of the promoter can be removed only after seeking approval of Reclassification from the Exchange. Meanwhile Companies are requested to show the promoters/promoter group with nil shareholding till the approval for Reclassification is granted from Exchange. 7. In case if the Company doesn’t have Significant Beneficiary owner, what details the Company has to give? In case if Company doesn’t have Significant Beneficiary owner, in declaration sheet the Company’s need to select No. 8. What has to be entered in case of Trust or HUF, i.e., name of the Trustee or Karta? The Company can give the name of the Trust or HUF, however in case of Promoter’s & Promoter’s Group consist of Trust or HUF then Company needs to enter the name of Trustee or Karta respectively in the bracket. 9. Can we upload the XML file of BSE for Shareholding Pattern? Yes, XML file generated from BSE utility file can be uploaded in NEAPS. Further in case of any problem faced while uploading you may email the error on nsexbrl@nse.co.in . Disclaimer: These guidelines are issued as guidance only. The directions/instructions issued in provision of Law, Regulation, SEBI and Exchange circular are referred to in these guidelines are
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued this circular on December 14, 2022 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2022/57) to all listed companies, updating its guidance in the form of FAQs on filing the shareholding pattern under Regulation 31 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, specifically on disclosure of holding of specified securities and dematerialized holdings. The circular does not create a new standalone legal regime, but it directs companies to comply with the listing regulations and any other applicable regulations as amended from time to time, and says the FAQs are for guidance only. It is aimed at improving the accuracy and consistency of the quarterly Shareholding Pattern report submitted to the Stock Exchange.

A key clarification is how to report deceased promoters or promoter group individuals: if an individual in the promoter or promoter group has died and the shares have not yet been transmitted to the legal heirs as of quarter-end, the company must continue to show the deceased person’s name in the promoter/promoter group section and add a detailed note explaining the situation. Once transmission is completed, the company may remove the deceased promoter’s name from subsequent shareholding pattern filings and must instead include the legal heir(s)’ name(s), again with a detailed note describing the transmission. If a promoter or promoter group company has been wound up or dissolved after merger/amalgamation, the company must add detailed notes in the shareholding pattern from the forthcoming quarter.

The circular also clarifies that a shareholder already disclosed in Table II, which covers promoter and promoter group shareholding, must not be repeated in Table III, which covers public shareholders; a person or entity that qualifies as promoter/promoter group should appear only in Table II and not again in Table III. Where a shareholder could fit more than one Table III category, the company must classify that holder only once, under the category that appears first in the prescribed shareholding-pattern format; shareholding categories must be unique and not duplicated. If a shareholder category contains multiple sub-categories, the number of shares must be separately reported under each relevant sub-category in column no. (XV) of Table III.

For changes in promoter status, the circular says a promoter’s name cannot be removed from the shareholding pattern merely because the shares were transferred or sold during the quarter; removal is allowed only after the stock exchange approves the reclassification request. Until that approval is granted, the company must continue showing the promoter/promoter group with nil shareholding. For disclosures on significant beneficial owners, if the company has none, it must select “No” in the declaration sheet. For trust or HUF holdings, the company may name the Trust or HUF itself, but if the promoter or promoter group consists of a Trust or HUF, it must also place the trustee’s name or karta’s name, respectively, in brackets.

Finally, the circular permits companies to upload the XML file generated from the BSE utility into NEAPS for shareholding-pattern filing; if there are upload issues, companies are instructed to email the error to nsexbrl@nse.co.in. The exchange’s disclaimer emphasizes that these FAQs are guidance only and do not override the legal requirements contained in the applicable law, SEBI regulations, or exchange circulars.

rows.title: Guidance note on inclusion of "object of the issue" in case of preferential issue and in Qualified institutions placement.
rows.desc: Circular Department: Download Ref No: NSE/CML/2022/56 Date: December 13, 2022 The Company Secretary All Listed Companies Subject: Guidance note on inclusion of “Object of the issue” in case of Preferential issues (in the Explanatory statement to the notice to the shareholders) and in Qualified Institutions Placement (“QIP”) (in the preliminary and final placement document) under Chapter V and VI of SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018, respectively. The SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018 was amended on November 21, 2022, to provide for, among other things, the requirement for appointing the SEBI registered Credit Rating Agency (“CRA”) as monitoring agency for monitoring the use of proceeds of such issues, if the issue size of QIP issue / Preferential issue exceeds one hundred crore rupees. It is observed that different issuers have used different ways for the disclosure of object of the issue in their related documents and in case of multiple objects, funds needed for each object is not indicated clearly. In view of the above, in order to ensure uniformity and enhance clarity in the disclosure of objects of the issue in case of QIP issue (Placement Document) and preferential issue (Notice to the shareholders), so that the CRAs can effectively monitor the utilisation of issue proceeds, the issuers are advised to ensure that they follow the guidelines prescribed below, while disclosing the object of issue in their Placement Document and Notice to the shareholders, as the case may be: a) The purpose for which fund is proposed to be raised shall be disclosed under the separate heading “Object of the issue”. b) Each object of the issue, for which funds are proposed to be raised shall be stated clearly and same shall not be open ended/ vague. c) The amount of funds proposed to be utilised against each of the object shall be stated clearly. In case, it is difficult to quantify the exact amount of fund to be used, a broad range of amount may be provided but the broad range shall be a realistic estimation and range gap shall not exceed +/- 10% of the amount specified for that object of issue size. Further, while giving broad range, the reason for providing the same shall be specified. d) Total amount of issue size allocated for different objects of the issue shall together be used only for the object of the issue as specified in the placement document/ notice to shareholders and same cannot be added to General Corporate Purposes (GCP). e) The tentative timeline for utilisation of issue proceeds for each of the object shall be clearly stated. Till such time the issue proceeds are fully utilised, the issuer shall also disclose the mode in which such funds will be kept. f) The fund to be used for General Corporate Purposes (GCP), if any, shall not exceed 25% of the funds to be raised through the preferential issue or QIP, under the current issue. The Exchange will be verifying compliance with the aforesaid disclosure requirements at the time of processing the application filed by the issuers under Regulation 28(1) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2018 seeking in- principle approval of the Exchange before making allotment of securities. Applicability: - The above guidance note will be applicable to all QIP and preferential issues which are approved by the Board of Directors of the issue on or after the date of issuance of this guidance note. Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Charmi Dharod Senior Manager
rows.summary:
This NSE guidance note, dated **December 13, 2022** and issued by the **National Stock Exchange of India Limited**, clarifies how listed companies must disclose the **“Object of the issue”** in documents relating to **preferential issues** and **Qualified Institutions Placements (QIPs)** under **Chapter V and Chapter VI of the SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018**. It was issued after the **November 21, 2022** amendment to the SEBI ICDR Regulations, which introduced a requirement to appoint a **SEBI-registered Credit Rating Agency (CRA)** as the **monitoring agency** for tracking utilization of issue proceeds where the issue size of a QIP or preferential issue **exceeds INR 100 crore**. The Exchange states that issuers have been using inconsistent disclosure formats and, especially where there are multiple objects, have not always made the funding requirement for each object clear enough for effective monitoring.

The guidance requires issuers to present the purpose of fund-raising under a separate heading titled **“Object of the issue”** in the **QIP placement document** and the **notice to shareholders for preferential issues**. Each object must be described **clearly and specifically**; vague or open-ended descriptions are not acceptable. The amount proposed to be used for each object must also be stated clearly. If an exact amount cannot be quantified, the issuer may provide a **broad range**, but that range must be a **realistic estimate**, must be supported by an explanation for using a range, and the range spread cannot exceed **plus/minus 10%** of the amount specified for that object.

The note also imposes restrictions on how proceeds are allocated and tracked: the total issue size earmarked for the identified objects must be used **only** for those stated objects and **cannot be shifted to General Corporate Purposes (GCP)**. If any amount is allocated to **GCP**, it cannot exceed **25% of the funds raised** in the relevant preferential issue or QIP. Issuers must additionally disclose the **tentative timeline** for using the proceeds for each object and specify **how unutilized funds will be held** until full deployment. These disclosure requirements are intended to support the CRA monitoring function for issues above the INR 100 crore threshold.

For compliance and processing purposes, the Exchange says it will check adherence to these disclosure requirements when reviewing applications under **Regulation 28(1) of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2018** for **in-principle approval** before allotment of securities. The guidance applies to **all QIP and preferential issues approved by the Board of Directors on or after December 13, 2022**.

rows.title: Circular for Seeking of comments, feedback on the XBRL for Regulation 30- OTS, ICA, Agreements, Fraud and Default
rows.desc: Circular Department: Listing Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2022/55 Date: November 22, 2022 The Company Secretary All Listed Companies Subject: Seeking of comments / feedback on the XBRL being introduced for submission of Announcements pertaining to: - One time settlement (OTS)/Inter-Creditors Agreement, - Agreements which are binding and not in normal course of business, revision(s) or amendment(s) and termination(s) thereof, - Fraud / Defaults by promoter or key managerial personnel or by the listed entity or arrest of key managerial personnel or promoter 1. OBJECTIVE: The objective of this document is to seek comments / feedback on the proposal to migrate from Portable Document Format (PDF) to eXtensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) format for submitting corporate announcements for - One time settlement (OTS)/Inter-Creditors Agreement, - Agreements which are binding and not in normal course of business, revision(s) or amendment(s) and termination(s) thereof, - Fraud / Defaults by promoter or key managerial personnel or by the listed entity or arrest of key managerial personnel or promoter as required under the provisions of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (LODR) read alongwith SEBI Circular dated September 09, 2015, as amended from time to time and such applicable laws. 2. BACKGROUND: Listed entities are required to submit periodical compliance filings to Stock Exchange(s) within prescribed timelines as laid down in SEBI Listing Regulations and accordingly, were mandated to report XBRL based filings for financials from year 2015 onwards. Over the period, Stock Exchanges in phased manner has been aiming to convert filings made under SEBI Regulations from PDF to XBRL. Listed entities file various disclosures under Regulation 30 of LODR with such details as are sought under the applicable Regulations/Circulars. With an objective to standardise securities market data it was deliberated that XBRL would be implemented for all corporate filings. Accordingly, Stock Exchanges have implemented XBRL based compliance filing mechanism featuring identical and homogenous compliance data structures which will not only ease the compliance burden on listed entities but also will enable analysis on the data submitted by the listed entities. Hence in this regard, filing of announcement pertaining to the aforementioned subjects, would require listed entities to file the same in XBRL exclusively, formats of which are made available in para 4 hereinbelow. 3. ISSUES AND DELIBERATIONS: Please note that the details required are typically descriptive in nature and based on the LODR provisions and applicable SEBI Circular. Accordingly, listed entities can provide their comments/feedback/suggestions/observations pertaining to any additions/modifications in the fields. 4. COMMENTS FROM LISTED ENTITIES Considering the implications of the XBRL filing by listed entities, comments in respect of the subject are solicited. Comments may be sent by email to DL-Announcement@nse.co.in in the following format: Name of entity / person: Contact Number & Email Address: Sr. No Event - One time settlement (OTS)/Inter-Creditors Agreement, - Agreements which are binding and not in normal course of business, revision(s) or amendment(s) and termination(s) thereof, - Fraud / Defaults by promoter or key managerial personnel or by the listed entity or arrest of key managerial personnel or promoter Subject/Heading/ Field Comments/ Suggestion Detailed Rationale While sending email, kindly mention the subject as “Comments / Feedback on the XBRL being introduced for OTS/ICA, Agreements, Fraud/Defaults” The comments may be sent by email to DL-Announcement@nse.co.in latest by November 28, 2022. Enclosed is the draft format for the XBRL being introduced for OTS/ICA, Agreements, Fraud/Defaults Yours faithfully, For National Stock Exchange of India Limited Dhaval Shah Manager – Listing Encl: Draft Format for XBRL being introduced for OTS/ICA, Agreements, Fraud/Defaults ONE TIME SETTLEMENT (OTS)/INTER-CREDITORS AGREEMENT POINT NO. PARTICULARS SUB-PARTICULARS 1 NSE Symbol 2 Name of the Company 3 BSE Scrip Code 4 MSE Symbol 5 ISIN 6 i. Type of Event I. Inter-Creditors Agreement (ICA) II. One time settlement ii. Stage at which the ICA Disclosure is made (Resolution plan / Restructuring in relation to loans / borrowings from banks / financial institutions) (a) Decision to initiate resolution of loans / borrowings; (b) Signing of Inter-Creditors Agreement (ICA) by lenders; (c) Finalization of Resolution Plan; (d) Implementation of Resolution Plan; (e) Salient features, not involving commercial secrets, of the resolution / restructuring plan as decided by lenders 7 Whether disclosure filed for listed company 8 Name of entity for which disclosure is filed 9 Relationship with the listed company 10 Date of Disclosure 11 Meeting in which One-time Settlement (OTS) is considered, if any 1. Board Meeting 2. Audit Committee Meeting 12 Date
rows.summary:
This circular, issued by NSE Listing Department on November 22, 2022 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2022/55), seeks feedback from all listed companies on a proposed shift from PDF to XBRL filing for certain Regulation 30 announcements under SEBI LODR. The specific disclosures proposed to become XBRL-only are: (1) one-time settlement (OTS) / inter-creditors agreements (ICA), (2) agreements that are binding but not in the ordinary course of business, including any revisions, amendments, or terminations of such agreements, and (3) frauds/defaults by a promoter, key managerial personnel, or the listed entity itself, including arrest of a promoter or key managerial personnel. The exchange says the objective is to standardize and structure these corporate disclosure data points so they can be filed in a uniform format, reduce compliance burden over time, and improve data analysis by the stock exchange; the proposal is aligned to SEBI LODR and the SEBI circular dated September 9, 2015, as amended.

The circular does not impose an immediate final filing rule in this document itself; rather, it invites comments, suggestions, and observations on the proposed XBRL fields and any additions or modifications needed. Feedback was requested by email to DL-Announcement@nse.co.in in a specified format containing the name of the entity/person, contact number and email address, the event category, the relevant subject/heading/field, the comment or suggestion, and the detailed rationale. The email subject line had to be: “Comments / Feedback on the XBRL being introduced for OTS/ICA, Agreements, Fraud/Defaults,” and comments were due no later than November 28, 2022.

The attached draft XBRL format shows the proposed data capture requirements for OTS/ICA disclosures. For such filings, the issuer would need to report identifiers such as NSE symbol, company name, BSE scrip code, MSE symbol, and ISIN, then specify the event type as either ICA or OTS. If the event is an ICA, the filer must also indicate the stage of disclosure, choosing from: decision to initiate resolution of loans/borrowings; signing of the ICA by lenders; finalization of the resolution plan; implementation of the resolution plan; or salient features of the resolution/restructuring plan decided by lenders, excluding commercial secrets. The draft also requires disclosure of whether the filing is being made for a listed company, the name of the entity for which the disclosure is filed, the relationship with the listed company, the disclosure date, and the meeting in which OTS was considered, if applicable, limited to Board Meeting or Audit Committee Meeting.

rows.title: Corrigendum on Standard Operating Process under SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (SDD)
rows.desc: National Stock Exchange of India Circular Department: LISTING Circular Ref No: NSE/CML/2022/52 Date: November 04, 2022 The Company Secretary All Listed Companies (Equity and/or Debt) Subject: Standard Operating Process under SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (SDD) This is in reference to the circular issued by the Exchange vide circular no. NSE/CML/2022/51 dated October 28, 2022. On Standard Operating Process under SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (SDD). Kindly note if company is not complied with the requirements of Reg 3(5) and 3(6) of SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 which required SDD to be maintained by the company, then Exchange shall initiate following action: Under the “Get Quote” page of the Exchange Website of the Listed Entity, wherever listed, would display that the company is non-compliant with SDD, from the next trading day till the Exchanges have satisfactorily verified that the company has completely complied. All Listed companies are requested to take note and comply accordingly. For and on behalf of National Stock Exchange of India Limited Yogesh Deshmukh Senior Manager
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a corrigendum/reference update to the Exchange’s earlier circular dated October 28, 2022 (NSE/CML/2022/51) on the Standard Operating Process under SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 relating to compliance with the Structured Digital Database (SDD) requirement. It applies to all listed companies on the NSE, including equity and/or debt listed entities.

The key requirement is that companies must comply with Regulations 3(5) and 3(6) of the SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015, which require maintenance of a Structured Digital Database by the company. If a company is found not to have complied with those SDD requirements, the Exchange will take enforcement action by displaying on the listed entity’s “Get Quote” page on the Exchange website that the company is non-compliant with SDD.

This disclosure will begin from the next trading day after the non-compliance is identified and will continue until the Exchange has satisfactorily verified that the company has fully complied with the SDD requirements. The circular does not introduce a new numerical threshold, rate, or deadline date beyond this “next trading day” trigger, but it does create an immediate market-facing consequence for non-compliance. Compliance teams should therefore ensure the company’s SDD is maintained in line with Reg. 3(5) and 3(6), because failure to do so can result in public non-compliance status being shown on the Exchange website until rectified and verified.
